items.body:
Codex desktop on Windows — three whole-application crashes in approximately four hours

Date: 14 October 2026. Timezone: Asia/Riyadh (UTC+03:00).
Installed package: OpenAI.Codex 26.1007.9446.0, Windows x64.
The owner reports similar exits almost daily while tasks are running.

Confirmed Crashpad sidecars:
- 13:31:57 — 0dbc09ae-aa6b-4d7a-9283-d63e34cdf580
- 15:01:08 — 8c267af1-6848-467a-84e4-3a7fc17d9f41
- 16:08:27 — 120e9415-6798-46a7-bb1f-62a429b40b13
All three contain capture_kind=crash, osarch=x86_64, ptype=browser.

Immediate pre-crash app log activity:
- 13:31:55: closing a browser-use tab, removal of its webview and guest teardown.
- 15:01:06: closing a browser-use tab; a concurrent lookup reports that the tab is not part of the browser session, followed by webview removal and guest teardown.
- 16:08:26: an in-app browser sidebar tab is opened/rebound.
The in-app browser lifecycle is a candidate trigger only. The records confirm crashes, but do not establish the exact native cause. No crash dump files remain in the inspected report directory.

No matching Windows Application Error/WER/Hang or resource-exhaustion records were returned for the queried last-five-hour interval. A later memory snapshot showed about4.76GiB physical memory and3.65GiB commit capacity available; this does not rule out earlier exhaustion. MCP startup/connection errors after restarting were observed separately and should not be mistaken for evidence of the whole-app crash cause.

Suggested temporary isolation: use an external browser for UI verification and avoid the embedded browser during active tasks, then see whether crashes recur. Do not delete app data or alter system memory/security settings as an unproven fix. This workaround has not yet been tested.

Please investigate the listed crash IDs and the app's embedded-browser tab-close/open lifecycle.

Diagnostic sources on the owner's computer:
%LOCALAPPDATA%/Codex/Logs/2026/10/14
%APPDATA%/Codex/web/Codex/Crashpad/reports

This summary excludes conversation content, access tokens, passwords and owner business data. It was prepared locally and has not been submitted or uploaded. No settings, cache, repository or owner database was changed.
Official feedback instructions: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/reference/troubleshooting#feedback-and-logs

### What version of the IDE extension are you using?

26.1007.21434

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Team

### Which IDE are you using?

Visual Studio Code

### What platform is your computer?

Windows — exact OS build not yet collected

### What issue are you seeing?

Codex in VS Code rejected an exec_command operation with this error:

exec_command failed: CreateProcess … Rejected(… rejected: blocked by policy)

The requested operation included starting a local Python engine for an Alpaca Paper trading simulation. This was explicitly authorized for simulated trading only, with no real-money trading authorized.

The rejection occurred at process creation, before any Alpaca API request. No specific policy identifier, detailed rejection reason, or actionable remediation was provided.

The session configuration reported approval_policy: never and danger-full-access. I do not know which component enforced the rejection or whether this is expected behavior.

Please clarify:
- Which component or policy rejected the operation?
- Is this an expected restriction or an IDE execution issue?
- What supported troubleshooting or review path is available?

Additional diagnostics:
- Registered engine version: 0.162.0-alpha.17.2
- Failure timestamp: October 14, 2026, approximately 04:41:55 UTC
- Tool call ID: call_2472952be4ca472cb0605578bcc8cb94

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed sequence (not a confirmed minimal reproduction):

1. Open the existing Python project in VS Code on Windows with the Codex extension.
2. Explicitly authorize starting the local engine in Alpaca Paper simulation mode only.
3. Codex attempts an exec_command operation that combines project checks, duplicate-process checks, starting paper_engine.py through PowerShell Start-Process, and a local panel health check.
4. Process creation is rejected with “blocked by policy,” without a detailed explanation.

The process-launch portion used the Python launcher with arguments:
-3.11 -B paper_engine.py

PowerShell Start-Process also included the project working directory, -WindowStyle Hidden, and -PassThru.

Expected behavior: either execute the authorized operation if permitted, or provide a specific rejection reason and a supported next step.

Actual behavior: generic process-creation rejection. The precise triggering part of the combined command has not been isolated.

### What is the expected behavior?

If the operation is permitted, Codex should start the explicitly authorized local Python process. If it is restricted, the extension should explain which policy or component blocked it and provide an actionable, supported troubleshooting or review path, rather than only “blocked by policy.”

### Additional information

The intended use is automated simulated trading through Alpaca Paper only. No real-money trading was authorized.

The error occurred during process creation, before any Alpaca API request. The available evidence does not establish whether the cause is an execution restriction, a configuration issue, or another policy layer.

I am requesting clarification and a supported resolution, not instructions to bypass restrictions. I can provide additional sanitized diagnostics if needed.

items.title: [macOS][Computer Use] Chrome pages go blank across Spaces; opening a new tab switches Spaces

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.1007.30912 (build 20156), read from the installed app bundle metadata.

This is the Codex surface of the desktop app. The installed bundle is named ChatGPT.app and has bundle identifier `com.openai.codex`.

### What subscription do you have?

Not specified in this report.

### What platform is your computer?

- macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), Apple Silicon
- `uname -mprs`: `Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 arm`
- Google Chrome 155.0.8059.80
- Native Chrome Computer Use through `cua_repl`
- Codex and the target Chrome window are on different macOS desktop Spaces.

### What issue are you seeing?

There are two reproducible problems when using Chrome through Codex Computer Use across macOS Spaces:

1. **After navigating or changing the page while the user stays on Codex's Space, the URL/title update correctly but the webpage content becomes blank.** The user sees a blank page in Codex's picture-in-picture preview, and the agent also receives a blank webpage screenshot. In the controlled reproduction, the accessibility state contains Chrome's toolbar and tabs but no webpage content or search controls. The agent can still perform some browser-toolbar operations, but cannot reliably inspect or interact with the page itself.
2. **Opening a new Chrome tab switches the user's active Space to Chrome's Space.** This interrupts whatever the user is doing in the other Space. We isolated this to a single Cmd+T operation: the Space switched before any URL was entered or navigation occurred.

Staying on Chrome's Space during the equivalent browsing operations allowed page capture, reading, and interaction to work.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

#### A. Blank webpage after navigation in an existing tab

1. Put Codex on one macOS Space and an open Chrome window on another.
2. Keep the user on Codex's Space. Have the agent reuse an existing Chrome tab.
3. In that tab, enter `https://www.wikipedia.org/` using Cmd+L, paste, and Return.
4. Inspect Codex's picture-in-picture preview and the agent's Chrome screenshot/accessibility state.
5. Use Chrome's Back and Forward buttons in that same tab, then try Cmd+R.

**Observed in this test:**

- The address text was verified before Return. The URL and title then changed to Wikipedia.
- The webpage area remained blank across subsequent captures. Fresh accessibility reads exposed browser controls but no Wikipedia search field or webpage content.
- Back navigated to the previous new-tab page; Forward returned to Wikipedia. These URL/control-state changes were observable, but the content area remained blank.
- Cmd+R did not restore the content. Whether a network reload actually occurred was not independently verified.
- Re-selecting Chrome through the tool also did not restore webpage content.
- The user confirmed they stayed on Codex's Space throughout this sequence, with **no automatic Space switch**. No new tab was created in this sequence.

**Control:** While the user stayed on Chrome's Space, the agent successfully followed example.com's “Learn more” link to IANA, opened Wikipedia, entered `Moon` in its search field, and reached `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moon`. Screenshots and accessibility content matched the loaded pages, and the search input was verified.

#### B. Opening a tab unexpectedly switches Spaces

1. Keep Codex and Chrome on separate Spaces, with the user currently on Codex's Space.
2. Have the agent send **only Cmd+T** to Chrome.
3. Observe the active Space before entering any URL.

**Observed:** A new blank tab was created, and the user confirmed an immediate automatic switch to Chrome's Space. The isolated tool action was:

```javascript
await chrome.pressKey('super+t');
```

As a separate control, sending only Cmd+L did not switch Spaces in this session. The address bar was already focused in that control, so it does not establish that every other keyboard operation preserves focus.

### What is the expected behavior?

- Page capture, accessibility information, and interaction should remain usable when the target Chrome window is on another macOS Space.
- Background Computer Use should preserve the user's active Space when opening tabs, so it does not interrupt work in another Space.
- If operating a window on another Space is unsupported, show a clear limitation and let the user choose how to proceed instead of silently returning blank page content.

### Additional information

- Reproduced on October 14, 2026 with public example.com, IANA, and Wikipedia pages.
- Avoiding new tabs does not resolve the blank-page problem: reproduction A used only an existing tab.
- Previously loaded static content was sometimes readable after re-selecting Chrome. This report concerns unreliable access after page changes, not a claim that every background read fails.
- The behavior is confirmed by both the user's Space/preview observations and the agent's screenshots/accessibility results. The underlying cause in macOS, Chrome, or Codex's capture/input path has not been established.
- Related report: #21668 concerns capturing the wrong window/Space. This report records a distinct observed outcome: the correct Chrome URL/title with blank webpage content, plus an isolated new-tab action that switches Spaces.

items.body:
## Summary

Codex desktop on Windows rejected an explicitly authorized, bounded read-only evidence-collection command before PowerShell or SSH started. The response gave only `CreateProcess` / `blocked by policy`, with no specific enforcing component, matching rule, or supported next step.

This report requests diagnosis and a supported resolution, not a policy exemption or safeguard bypass. Full-access settings and user authorization are not claimed to override other security controls.

## Environment and evidence provenance

- Component: Codex desktop on native Windows.
- App/package version: `26.1007.9446.0`, derived from the running application's installed package path during later local read-only inspection; not read from an About dialog.
- Codex version recorded in the original failed session: `0.162.0-alpha.17.2`.
- Windows: Windows 10 Pro Education, 22H2, build `19045.7725`, x64.
- Later local diagnostic host: PowerShell `7.6.5`. The denied PowerShell process itself never started.
- Subscription, failure-time app elevation, and applicable managed/MDM requirements: not established.

## Exact incident identifiers

- Command submission: `2026-10-14T10:01:21.663Z` (18:01:21.663, Asia/Shanghai, UTC+08:00).
- Rejection response: `2026-10-14T10:01:21.753Z`.
- Outer `functions.exec` call ID: `call_71fdce3b9d9b4afbab5efab491831667`.
- A separate inner `exec_command` invocation ID was not supplied.
- Successfully submitted in-app feedback ID: `019eee82-ee9c-7d90-8b01-a9344ef2e49b`.

Sanitized error excerpt, not the full original command or raw transcript:

```text
exec_command failed: CreateProcess
Rejected(<command redacted> rejected: blocked by policy)
```

## Effective settings in the original failed turn

These values were read from the original turn-context record associated with the call, not inferred from the current UI or a later configuration file:

```text
sandbox_policy.type = danger-full-access
permission_profile.type = disabled
active_permission_profile.id = :danger-full-access
approval_policy = never
approvals_reviewer = user
```

No actionable approval prompt was exposed. Since the recorded approval policy was `never`, the absence of an interactive prompt is not itself asserted to be a bug.

## Intended operation and actual outcome

The intended command was an in-memory PowerShell/.NET workflow, bounded to one SSH connection for a fixed source-file read and four anonymous document GETs. It was not authorized to modify remote files or a database, submit forms, purge caches, deploy, delete data, or explicitly save local evidence files. Private paths, hosts, arguments, environment values, and source code are intentionally omitted here.

This is a description of the original incident, not a newly executed minimal reproducer.

- Process creation was refused.
- PowerShell/SSH startup and the intended remote requests did not occur.
- No native process exit code or native stdout/stderr exists for this denied launch; these are NOT RUN, not exit 0 or empty captured streams.
- The denied command was not resubmitted, split, rerouted, or retried with broader permissions.

## Later read-only inspection and limitations

- Independent local inspection succeeded; that does not prove the denied command was permitted or identify its rejecting rule.
- The current local configuration specifies Windows sandbox `elevated`; it is not presented as proof that this implementation governed the original full-access turn.
- The readable local command-rule file contained 47 `allow` entries and no detected `prompt` or `forbidden` decisions. This is not managed/platform-policy clearance.
- The expected `.sandbox/sandbox.log` was absent. Available dated sandbox logs ended on October 13; no corresponding October 14 sandbox log was found.
- No secret-directory contents, credentials, raw logs, session files, screenshots, private configuration, or business/source data are attached to this public issue.

## Related reports and deduplication

Similar symptoms were reported in #53977 and #53215, but those are different incidents. A shared root cause has not been established. Repository searches for this report's feedback ID and outer call ID returned no existing issue at submission time.

## Requested guidance

1. Using the incident and feedback identifiers, identify the component and restriction that rejected this invocation.
2. Explain whether this is an intended restriction or an unintended match; the available record cannot determine that.
3. Provide the supported resolution/review route, or specify the minimum additional sanitized evidence needed.

Please do not suggest treating Full Access, changing execution channels, or broad permission expansion as a bypass. No further reproduction, production access, or configuration changes are being performed under this report.

labels.name: bug

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.1007.21434 — last observed in local desktop logs on October 13, 2026; not rechecked in About for every October 14 failure.

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT subscription; account usage response reports planType: prolite.

### What platform is your computer?

Windows (Codex desktop app).

### What issue are you seeing?

## Summary
On October 14, 2026 (Asia/Shanghai, UTC+8), I encountered HTTP 429 errors in multiple different tasks in the Windows Codex desktop app. The problem is not confined to the original long conversation.

When account usage was queried during troubleshooting, the weekly allowance showed 30% used (approximately 70% remaining), and ordinaryUsageAllowed was true. This is not evidence that all rate limits were clear: other short-term or service-side limits may still apply. The UI did not explain which limit caused this rejection.

## Environment
- Product: Codex desktop app on Windows, signed in with a ChatGPT account.
- Last locally observed desktop release: 26.1007.21434 (from October 13 logs; not independently rechecked for every October 14 failure).
- Model observed in the affected task's connection-error logs: gpt-6-astra, medium reasoning. The model has not been verified for every task that returned 429.
- Date of the cross-task 429 reports: October 14, 2026, UTC+8.

## Error evidence
The screenshot shows:

```text
exceeded retry limit, last status: 429 Too Many Requests, request id: 0337d3e0-508f-4957-b3fe-5fb57422af83
```

The UI also shows “已处理 6分钟47秒” (processed for 6 minutes 47 seconds) and “服务器繁忙，正在重新连接 1/5” (server busy, reconnecting 1/5). The screenshot does not provide an exact wall-clock time.

The account usage query returned:
- Weekly window: 10080 minutes.
- usedPercent: 30 (about 70% remaining).
- ordinaryUsageAllowed: true.
- rateLimitReachedType: null.
- spendControlReached: false.
- No secondary window was returned by this query. This should not be read as proof that no other limit exists.



### What steps can reproduce the bug?

## Observed behavior / reproduction limits
1. Use existing tasks in Windows Codex Desktop.
2. Some turns stall and display connection/retry messages.
3. Multiple different tasks returned HTTP 429 on the same day.
4. Checking account usage still showed approximately 70% of the weekly allowance available.

This is a report of observed intermittent behavior, not a deterministic minimal reproduction. I have captured the request ID above; request IDs from all the other affected tasks have not yet been collected.



### What is the expected behavior?

## Expected behavior / requested investigation
- Please correlate the request ID with backend logs and identify the specific limit or service condition responsible.
- If this is a short-term rate limit, show the affected limit and an actionable retry time, distinguishing it from exhausted weekly allowance.
- If it is a service-side issue, please confirm and track it.
- Please clarify why the UI shows both “server busy” and “exceeded retry limit” without identifying the applicable limit.



### Additional information

## Related connection failures
During this troubleshooting period, the app also displayed:

```text
stream disconnected before completion: websocket closed by server before response.completed
stream disconnected before completion: IO error: 远程主机强迫关闭了一个现有的连接。 (os error 10054)
```

Local logs recorded WebSocket retries followed by HTTP fallback. A fresh conversation initially worked, but failures later recurred. I cannot establish that the connection failures and the 429s share one root cause, or that conversation length caused the 429s. Cross-network comparison and request concurrency have not been controlled.


## Related reports and support history
- #30471 discusses the same 429 error wording; this report concerns observed cross-task failures with weekly allowance still remaining, not a claim that the source-level issue proves our root cause.
- #18960 contains similar WebSocket reconnect reports.
- I submitted this evidence to the OpenAI Help Center support conversation. Its AI support confirmed the message was recorded but said it could not query backend logs, confirm engineering acceptance, or transfer the conversation to human support. No engineering ticket number has been provided.

No email address, account ID, private task IDs, project names, local file paths, creative content, or full logs are included in this public report.

## Problem
In Codex desktop on Windows, an authorized local diagnostic command was rejected before PowerShell started. The returned error was `exec_command failed: CreateProcess ... rejected: blocked by policy`, with wall time 0.0 seconds and no process exit code or stdout. This prevented installation of a prepared local application change. The same command was rejected again after the user explicitly authorized the operation.

## Evidence
- 2026-10-14 11:50:16.600 UTC — tool call `call_b0e86c4a023d4bffa5bac0d59aa38b53`
- 2026-10-14 11:51:18.068 UTC — tool call `call_d5042fde70704e1a9e46b248d01a16d2`

- Active turn context: `approval_policy=never`, `sandbox_policy=danger-full-access`, model `gpt-6-astra`, effort `high`.
- The command combined three read-only checks: search for process-management keywords inside a local script using `rg`; GET a local `127.0.0.1` status endpoint; and read a local service identity JSON. `Start-Process` and `Stop-Process` appeared as `rg` search terms, not as executed commands.
- Other shell commands run normally in the same environment. A later local endpoint check returned HTTP 200, and a TLS connection to the mail provider succeeded. No evidence that the blocked command reached the local service or network.
- The OpenAI status incident affecting Codex and ChatGPT Work on 2026-10-14 was marked resolved before the two denials above. We cannot establish whether it is related.

## Request
Please identify which policy component/rule rejected these calls, whether this is an unintended match or expected restriction, and the supported way to review and resolve such denials in Codex desktop. The user wants to continue authorized local development without weakening security settings or routing around a rejected command.

No mail contents, credentials, private file paths, or raw logs are included. The exact command and underlying session record can be reviewed by OpenAI using the identifiers above.

items.body:
### Environment

- Windows 11, Codex desktop.
- Desktop package version observed in same-day error logs: `26.1007.2314.0`.
- Separately installed npm CLI: `codex-cli 0.160.0`. The desktop-bundled CLI version was not established.
- Audit date: 2026-10-14.

### Observed problem

Codex marketplace update staging consumed **286.85 GiB** on C:, including **93.21 GiB of surviving files created overnight** (2026-10-13 18:00 through 2026-10-14 10:00, UTC+04:00). C: became full; Codex logged `ENOSPC: no space left on device, write` and Docker Desktop failed to write its startup log.

Affected path:

`%USERPROFILE%\.codex\.tmp\marketplaces\.staging\marketplace-upgrade-*`

Measured evidence:

- 1,074 staging directories, 5,769,445 files, **308,002,150,436 logical bytes**.
- 1,039 directory manifests identify `gitnexus-marketplace` and contain GitNexus repository checkouts.
- Other manifests: eight `claude-plugins-official`, two `ponytail`, one `caveman`; 24 incomplete/unidentified.
- 257 staging directories were created during the overnight window.
- Overnight surviving file size: **100,079,210,070 logical bytes**.
- Oldest surviving staging directory: 2026-07-25. Newest: 2026-10-14 08:43, UTC+04:00.
- Full scan of the Codex temporary tree reported zero read errors.
- Multiple overnight Git packs are about 110 MB each; staging includes repeated repository working trees as well as Git objects.

Configured source:

```toml
[marketplaces.gitnexus-marketplace]
source_type = "git"
source = "https://github.com/abhigyanpatwari/GitNexus.git"
```

### Attribution and limits

The staging accumulation is confirmed. Background marketplace refresh activity is the likely source, but the exact retry/activation/cleanup failure was not captured live. This report does **not** establish that GitNexus plugin code is malicious or that every upgrade fails. Recent conversation transcripts did not contain an explicit marketplace-upgrade command. Historical directories span multiple app versions.

These are current surviving logical sizes, not a before/after disk-allocation measurement. We have not intentionally reproduced the leak or deleted the evidence.

### Expected behavior

Successful, failed and interrupted marketplace operations should leave bounded temporary storage, with safe recovery/cleanup for abandoned staging directories. Repeated refreshes should not accumulate hundreds of full repository copies or fill the system drive without warning.

### Related reports

#21005, #29994 and #45943 describe similar staging accumulation. This adds a current Windows desktop occurrence with GitNexus and measured overnight growth. Please consolidate if this is the same tracked defect.

Only sanitized technical measurements are included; no credentials, usernames, private project paths or raw transcripts.

labels.name: bug

labels.name: windows-os

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: connectivity
labels.description: Issues involving networking or endpoint connectivity problems (disconnections)

items.body:
## Summary

On Windows, new chats in both ChatGPT Work and Codex cannot send messages. The composer accepts text, but the Send button stays disabled. The Codex home screen displays:

> 无法加载工作空间设置
> 请重试以继续聊天

English: "Couldn't load workspace settings / Retry to continue chatting."

The user reports that the web version works. This existing desktop conversation remains usable, but new-chat initialization is blocked.

## Environment

- Windows desktop application
- App version: **26.1007.71326**
- App build: **20398**, channel **prod**
- Windows package version: **26.1007.9446.0** (distinct from the app version)
- In-app updater reports **up_to_date**
- Execution location shown in the screenshot: **This computer**
- Observed on **2026-10-14**

## Steps to reproduce on the affected installation

1. Open a new chat in the Windows desktop application.
2. Select local execution ("This computer").
3. Enter a simple message such as `111`.
4. The Send arrow remains greyed out.
5. In Codex, the workspace-settings error banner is visible. The issue also affects starting a Work chat.

Expected: workspace settings initialize and a message can be submitted.
Actual: new chats remain blocked before a task begins.

## Sanitized diagnostic evidence

Desktop logs around **2026-10-14 20:05 Asia/Shanghai (12:05 UTC)** repeatedly record HTTP **403** with `errorCode=cloudflare_challenge` and `errorMessage=cloudflare_challenge` for routes including:

- `/accounts/check/{version}`
- `/accounts/optimized/check`
- `/settings/user`
- `/profiles/me`

Cloud WebSocket connections also repeatedly close before establishment. The local app-server connection is recorded as connected.

These are observed failures during the affected period. They do not establish which request is the sole cause of the composer block, or prove an account entitlement or workspace policy denial.

## Checks and attempted recovery

- Retrying and reopening the desktop app have not restored new-chat submission.
- The account's Codex usage query reports `ordinaryUsageAllowed=true`; this alone does not establish every Work entitlement.
- The existing local system proxy was backed up, enabled, and system network settings refreshed.
- The reopened app continued to record the same HTTP 403 challenge errors.
- Read-only inspection found a global proxy route rather than an observed separate desktop-client route.
- The updater offers no further update on this installation.

No application data, conversation history, credentials, or workspace policy flags were deleted or bypassed. No successful new-chat recovery has been verified.

## Related reports and request

Related: #51917, #53384, #53609. This provides another affected installation on app **26.1007.71326**.

Please investigate desktop account/workspace initialization and challenge recovery, especially the difference between working existing conversations or web access and blocked desktop new chats. A supported recovery procedure that preserves conversations and policy enforcement would be helpful.

This report contains only selected diagnostic fields and UI observations. No account identifiers, emails, credentials, cookies, proxy secrets, private paths, full logs, documents, or conversation contents are attached.

Issue:
Previously pasted text disappears from the Codex desktop app composer while entering Japanese using romaji input.

3. Immediately type t, then t, then e to compose “って”.

- The same input sequence does not cause the problem in Sublime Text.
- Clibor was not running during testing.

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os

labels.name: tool-calls

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

Version 26.1007.71326

### What subscription do you have?

pro 200

### What platform is your computer?

windows 11

### What issue are you seeing?

## Description

Codex Desktop on Windows consistently fails to initialize Computer Use (CUA) when invoked through Dot-delegated sessions.

The failure occurs immediately during MXC launcher initialization, before the browser can be accessed.

**Exact error:**

```
MXC launcher: cannot locate required Windows platform directory: HRESULT 0x80070003
```

Additional diagnostic output:

```
node_repl kernel exited unexpectedly
kernel_status: exited(code=1)
```

## Environment

- Operating system: Windows (exact build not yet collected)
- Codex Desktop: 26.1007.71326
- Previous version: 26.1007.21434
- Execution route: Dot-delegated Codex session
- MXC sandbox: Enabled; no changes made
- Application: Codex Desktop for Windows

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open Codex Desktop on Windows.
2. Connect Dot to the computer through the supported delegation workflow.
3. Have Dot initiate a harmless CUA browser-state or tab-list request.
4. Observe that initialization fails before browser information can be retrieved.

## Actual result

On version 26.1007.71326, the browser-state attempt failed after approximately 0.263 seconds with HRESULT 0x80070003.

The same error was observed before upgrading from 26.1007.21434.

Rebooting Windows did not resolve the issue.

A separate direct Codex session successfully controlled Chrome through its attached DevTools browser connection, suggesting this is specific to certain execution paths rather than a general inability to run Chrome.

However, direct CUA initialization has also timed out in an earlier diagnostic.

## Suspected cause

Investigations in existing Codex GitHub issues suggest that Windows environment variables, particularly `SystemDrive` and `LOCALAPPDATA`, may not be propagated correctly into Dot-delegated execution environments.

Affected users have captured child processes missing these variables. An unresolved `%SystemDrive%\ProgramData` path has been associated with HRESULT 0x80070003.

Independent reproduction tests support this failure mechanism, but we have not verified the exact environment of the failing process on this particular installation.

This may indicate a Codex process-launch environment-filtering defect rather than a Windows operating system failure.

## Troubleshooting completed

- Upgraded Codex Desktop to 26.1007.71326.
- Repeated a single read-only CUA initialization test.
- Confirmed that the exact error persists.
- Previously rebooted Windows without improvement.
- Verified that Chrome DevTools browser control works through a separate execution route.

No MXC security settings were disabled. No runtime patches, application resets, or session deletions were performed.

## Related issues

- #52407
- #53188
- #53255
- #52857

## Impact

This issue blocks Dot from supervising browser-dependent development work on our Windows workstation.

Multiple active business application projects are affected because automated browser access and acceptance testing cannot proceed.

## Requested investigation

Please investigate whether the Dot-delegated CUA/MXC process launcher is incorrectly filtering required Windows environment variables.

We would appreciate:

1. Confirmation of the root cause.
2. An official fix for the environment-variable propagation issue.
3. A supported diagnostic procedure.
4. A workaround that preserves MXC sandbox security and existing session history.
5. Confirmation of which Windows Desktop release contains the repair.

This problem remains reproducible after updating to Codex Desktop 26.1007.71326.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Install and open Codex Desktop for Windows, version `26.1007.71326`.
2. Start a new Codex session on the Windows computer, preferably through Dot delegation.
3. Allow the session to initialize using its normal Windows sandbox and default security settings.
4. Ask Codex to execute this harmless PowerShell command:

   ```powershell
   Write-Output 'CODEX_SHELL_OK'
   ```

5. Observe that the command produces no stdout, stderr, or exit code after 10 seconds.
6. Interrupt the stalled command. In our test, interruption returned exit code 1.
7. Repeat once using:

   ```powershell
   Write-Output PREFLIGHT_OK
   ```

8. Observe that the second command also hangs without output or an exit code, even after 30 seconds.

### Actual Behavior

Basic PowerShell commands hang indefinitely or until interrupted. No output or exit status is returned during execution.

This failure occurs before any repository operations begin.

### Expected Behavior

Both PowerShell commands should complete almost immediately, print their respective text markers, and return exit code 0.

### Environment

- OS: Windows
- Codex Desktop: `26.1007.71326`
- Execution: Dot-delegated Windows session
- Shell: PowerShell
- Sandbox: Existing/default configuration, unchanged
- No STELLA repository modifications

### Additional Information

The same failure was previously observed before updating Codex Desktop. Updating to `26.1007.71326` did not resolve it.

Related GitHub issues: #39574, #50725, #51882.

The underlying cause is not confirmed. The failure could involve process launching, command dispatch, or result delivery in Codex Desktop.

### What is the expected behavior?

Codex Desktop should preserve the Windows environment information required to initialize supported Computer Use processes.

Dot-delegated CUA operations should successfully initialize the browser-control environment, read browser state, enumerate tabs, and perform authorized interactions without HRESULT 0x80070003.

Updating Codex Desktop should preserve existing conversations, worktrees, settings, and security protections.

If initialization fails, Codex should return actionable diagnostic information identifying the missing dependency or failed launcher operation.

### Additional information

Codex Desktop version: 26.1007.71326
Previous version: 26.1007.21434

CUA failure duration: 0.263 seconds

Error:
MXC launcher: cannot locate required Windows platform directory: HRESULT 0x80070003

Additional output:
node_repl kernel exited unexpectedly
kernel_status: exited(code=1)

Result:
CUA initialization failed before reading browser state.

items.title: Avoid reconnect races in the daemon restart test
items.body:
Avoid reconnect races in the daemon restart test

## Why

PTY reads can split a redraw while the reconnect notice is temporarily erased. The test can then submit `/status` before reconnection finishes, when Enter is suppressed.

## What changed

Make the `discovered` daemon startup test inspect only completed synchronized terminal updates. Type `/status` separately from Enter and wait for its command popup before submitting. Gate both inputs on a replacement daemon PID and the absence of the reconnect notice.

items.title: Google Drive plugin: support link sharing and notifications for non-Google recipients

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: skills
labels.description: Issues related to skills

items.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

Codex desktop on macOS (Darwin 27.0.0, arm64), installed Google Drive plugin version 0.1.20, using the connected-app tool `mcp__codex_apps__google_drive_share_file`.

### What feature would you like to see?

Expose two Google Drive sharing options through the connected plugin:

1. Explicit notification control for named recipients, including `sendNotificationEmail=true` when Google requires an invitation for an email address without a Google account.
2. Explicit, read-only "anyone with the link" access (`type=anyone`, `role=reader`, `allowFileDiscovery=false`).

The use case is API-only delivery of uploaded archives to external recipients. The user has explicitly authorized sharing. Upload, metadata reads and downloading work, but sharing to a non-Google recipient is blocked by the tool's available parameters. A browser login should not be necessary to expose these operations when the connected account is already authenticated and permitted to share.

### Reproduction and actual behavior

The current tool schema exposes `url`, `permission`, `user_email`, `anyone_at_company` and `show_in_search`. It offers neither a notification flag nor permission type `anyone`.

With an uploaded file owned by the connected account, call the tool for a recipient without a Google account:

```json
{
  "url": "https://drive.google.com/file/d/<FILE_ID>/view",
  "permission": "reader",
  "user_email": "recipient@example.com"
}
```

The returned Google error shows a permissions request with `sendNotificationEmail=False`:

```text
POST https://www.googleapis.com/drive/v3/files/<FILE_ID>/permissions
  ?supportsAllDrives=True&sendNotificationEmail=False&allowFileDiscovery=False

HTTP 400 invalidSharingRequest:
You are trying to invite recipient@example.com. Since there is no Google
account associated with this email address, you must check the "Notify
people" box to invite this recipient.
```

Trying to obtain link access by omitting the recipient also fails:

```json
{
  "url": "https://drive.google.com/file/d/<FILE_ID>/view",
  "permission": "reader",
  "anyone_at_company": false,
  "show_in_search": false
}
```

```text
ValueError: Either user or anyone_at_company must be specified
```

All recipient addresses and file IDs above are placeholders.

### Expected behavior

Allow the caller to request a named-recipient invitation with notifications enabled, subject to Google Workspace visitor-sharing policy. Separately, allow explicit anyone-with-link reader permission where account policy permits it. For `type=anyone`, omit `sendNotificationEmail`, since Google's API does not allow that parameter for this permission type.

Keep public link sharing opt-in, preserve `allowFileDiscovery=false` by default, and return the resulting permission and usable link so access can be verified before delivery.

Google API references:

- [permissions.create](https://developers.google.com/workspace/drive/api/reference/rest/v3/permissions/create): supports notification control for user/group permissions.
- [Permission resource](https://developers.google.com/workspace/drive/api/reference/rest/v3/permissions): supports `type=anyone` and `allowFileDiscovery`.

### Source and routing

The installed plugin manifest points to [openai/plugins](https://github.com/openai/plugins/tree/main/plugins/google-drive). Its public package contains manifests, skills and configuration; I could not locate the hosted connected-app `share_file` implementation there. Issues are disabled on that repository, so this report is filed here. Please route to the connected Google Drive tool owner if its implementation is maintained elsewhere. This report concerns the connected-app tool, not a verified defect in the separate Google-hosted Drive MCP server.

labels.name: bug

items.body:
## Summary

Several recent Windows reports describe Codex failing to import its bundled Browser/Chrome client with `EPERM: operation not permitted, realpath`. In the browser-specific reports, the failure happens before Browser setup, browser selection, or the Chrome/Edge extension handshake. The file is reported as present and readable, while native path resolution fails inside the sandbox.

This issue is an umbrella to help track the reports together. The reports suggest a Windows sandbox/AppContainer path-canonicalization problem, but a shared root cause has not been confirmed.

## Common evidence across the reports

- The error occurs while importing `browser-client.mjs`, before any page or browser connection is reached.
- Multiple reports distinguish successful stat/read or non-native path resolution from failing native `realpath` in MXC/AppContainer.
- Reports include Windows API comparisons where DOS/GUID final-path resolution fails while NT/no-volume resolution succeeds.
- One report reproduces the same native `realpath` failure for files inside an authorized writable workspace, suggesting the issue may extend beyond the browser plugin.
- Chrome and Edge are both affected in at least one report.

These observations point toward the Windows sandbox/module-loading boundary. They do not establish that the Chrome extension itself is defective or that all linked reports share one cause. In particular, the runtime provisioning/file-locking symptom reported in #51972 may be separate.

## Direct reports of the browser import / native realpath failure

- [#51669 — Chrome/Browser client fails with EPERM before extension handshake](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/51669) (first report found; Oct 7)
- [#51972 — Browser bootstrap EPERM; also reports runtime provisioning locks](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/51972)
- [#52593 — Native realpath fails inside a writable workspace](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/52593)
- [#53045 — Browser tool fails under MXC for both Chrome and Edge](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/53045)
- [#53332 — Built-in Browser import fails under MXC](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/53332)
- [#53638 — AppContainer returns EPERM loading browser-client.mjs](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/53638)

## Related Windows Chrome integration reports; failure mode may differ

- [#39399 — Browser/Chrome plugin trusted RPC dependency path validation](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/39399)
- [#53171 — Chrome extension reports app missing because the registered native host executable is absent](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/53171)
- [#38510 — Chrome native-host cache retry loop causes CPU usage and input lag](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/38510)

## Request

Please investigate whether the direct realpath reports share a Windows sandbox/module-loader cause, identify a canonical tracking issue, and mark only confirmed duplicates as duplicates. Please keep the distinct native-host deployment, trusted-RPC, and retry-loop failures separate if they require different fixes.

Any fix should preserve sandbox isolation; disabling sandbox protections or broadening filesystem permissions is not an acceptable workaround.

### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.1007.71326 (Build 20398); originally 26.1007.21434 (Build 13901)

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro

### What platform is your computer?

Windows x64

### What issue are you seeing?

Publishing an existing Site is blocked in the Codex Windows desktop app.

With “Ask for approval” enabled, after approving network access and write access to the repository Git directory, write_stdin failed with:

write_stdin rejected: approval required by policy, but AskForApproval::Granular.sandbox_approval is false

No additional approval prompt appeared. A full restart did not resolve this on version 26.1007.21434 (Build 13901).

After updating to 26.1007.71326 (Build 20398), a fresh Site workflow helper accepted stdin, but repository access failed:

fatal: unable to access https://git.chatgpt-team.site/[repository path redacted]/: Failed to connect to git.chatgpt-team.site port 443: Could not connect to server

A later Test-NetConnection resolved the hostname but returned TcpTestSucceeded: False. A separate git ls-remote attempt then failed with:

git: remote-https is not a git command.
fatal: remote helper https aborted session

The Git selected by the command runner is the bundled Codex runtime Git. git-remote-https.exe was not found at its reported exec-path. The reason has not been established. The session currently has restricted network access and no request_permissions tool, so these checks do not prove a remote server outage or that the original failure is fixed after a network permission grant.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Use the Windows desktop app with Ask for approval enabled.
2. Ask the agent to publish an existing Site.
3. Approve the requested network and repository Git-directory permissions.
4. Start the supported Site workflow helper in an interactive terminal; it waits for JSON on stdin.
5. Call write_stdin to provide the input. On the original version, it is rejected with the approval-policy error before delivery. Even an empty JSON object is rejected in that session.
6. A separate basic stdin test without the additional grant succeeds.
7. After the app update and restart, the helper accepts stdin but fails connecting to the repository host. A subsequent read-only git ls-remote fails because the HTTPS remote helper is unavailable.

### What is the expected behavior?

Granted permissions should permit the operation, or an actionable approval prompt should appear. The supported Site workflow should be able to reach its source repository, and the bundled Git installation should include the HTTPS remote helper it needs.

### Additional information

Feedback ID: 01a02d9d-8711-7433-ac3a-571c5c205f23

Related reports: #53134, #52210, #53610. The reporter of #53610 closed it after switching to a web browser; this does not establish a desktop fix. This report adds the observed behavior after updating and the bundled Git/network errors.

The Site update remains unpublished. No credentials or customer data are included.

items.title: Windows Codex Desktop: silent browser-main exits during concurrent tasks, with captured memory surge

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

items.body:
## User impact

Codex Desktop intermittently disappears without a warning during ordinary work on several concurrent tasks. Active tasks are interrupted. Opening or switching other chats can also become unresponsive. UI stuttering and instant full application exits are distinct symptoms: the application need not visibly hang immediately before an exit.

The requested outcome is reliable concurrent work and chat switching within the official desktop application, with preservation of active work. A separate terminal interface or disabling the user's normal workflow is not an acceptable resolution.

## Installed environment and update verification

- Windows 11 Pro x64, build 26200.
- Intel Core Ultra 7 155H; approximately 15.47 GiB OS-visible physical RAM.
- Current desktop product release: 26.1007.71326, build 20398, production channel.
- Current registered and running Microsoft Store package: OpenAI.Codex 26.1007.9446.0.
- Bundled backend: codex-cli 0.162.0-alpha.17.2.
- The package reports Status=Ok and SignatureKind=Store.
- The official desktop update checker reports up_to_date for the configured updater/channel.

The earlier package 26.1007.2314.0 / app 26.1007.21434 was updated successfully on October 14, 2026, at 10:46:45 Europe/Warsaw. The executable path was checked to verify that the newer registered package was actually running. The update did not eliminate subsequent browser-main crashes.

## Confirmed crashes

All times below are October 14, 2026, Europe/Warsaw (UTC+2).

- 09:40:10: Crashpad sidecar, browser main, before the update.
- 10:26:16: a native minidump was captured locally before the SDK removed its original copy.
- 12:28:48: a subsequent Crashpad browser-main sidecar on the updated installation.
- 12:53:45: another Crashpad browser-main sidecar on the updated installation.

Sidecars identify capture_kind=crash, osarch=x86_64, ptype=browser. These are full main-process exits, not merely a renderer reload. No full dump was retained for the two post-update crashes, so their exception codes are not asserted to match the earlier captured dump.

## Memory evidence for the captured pre-update crash

A separate, lightweight local recorder sampled the same main process every five seconds. It survived the application exit.

| Local time | Main-process private memory, MiB | Available physical memory, MiB |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 10:25:27 | 574.4 | 2473.7 |
| 10:25:37 | 980.0 | 2538.2 |
| 10:25:47 | 1702.6 | 2125.6 |
| 10:25:57 | 3818.4 | 198.1 |
| 10:26:02 | 4213.1 | 13.9 |
| 10:26:12 | 4507.4 | 50.6 |
| 10:26:17 | 4524.6 | 690.6 |

The main process was gone by the next sample and available RAM recovered to approximately 6709 MiB. This establishes a rapid main-process memory surge associated with that crash; it does not identify the retained object, allocation site, or triggering RPC.

The retained minidump is approximately 45.65 MB. Manual structural inspection found:

- Exception code: 0x80000003.
- Faulting module: chrome.dll, offset 0x3afce8d, from the earlier package.
- Exception thread: CrBrowserMain.
- Stack-referenced strings include owl/common/node_bindings.cc and CALL_AND_RETRY_LAST.

These observations should be symbolized against the matching release by maintainers. String references alone are not presented as a recovered complete fatal error message.

## Other measured pressure

Desktop logs contain many AppServerConnection request-queue rejections, including mcpServer/tool/call with approximately three in-flight requests and twenty queued interactive requests. The message shown to clients is that the app-server request queue is full. Renderer logs also repeatedly report ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications. These are accompanying symptoms; a shared causal chain with the native crash has not been proved.

Two frequently used histories have grown to approximately 2.69 GB and 4.49 GB. Both use paginated history and their projection offsets are populated. Their size is not, by itself, evidence of corruption or the native crash trigger.

## Reversible local changes and their verification limits

- Increased supported automatic PR polling interval to 300 seconds.
- Removed a verified stale attachment to a missing worktree using the app-server attachment API.
- Corrected a local synchronization fallback reader that repeatedly scanned complete multi-GB JSONL histories. It now validates indexed task-start offsets and reads the required suffix through EOF, including newly appended records. Comparison tests passed for latest-six turns, a specific old turn, stale index, invalid offset and missing index. A real latest-six read took 1.74 seconds.
- Temporarily paused a five-minute synchronization heartbeat for isolation, then restored its original schedule and prompt. Current status is ACTIVE.
- No application bundle, native DLL, integrity fuse or vendor signature was modified. No history database was edited directly or reset.

After re-enabling the heartbeat, an in-app navigation check opened two large existing chats and another chat, then returned to the diagnostic chat. The same main process and backend processes remained running. Sampled main private memory was 394–419 MiB and logged history-page fetches were 13–19 ms. This is a short successful check, not proof that intermittent crashes or UI stuttering are fixed.

## Requested investigation

Please correlate the captured fatal main-process exception and memory trajectory with matching native symbols and main-process heap/transport instrumentation. Investigate whether large-history or concurrent tool/update handling can cause an unbounded allocation, and identify the source of request-queue saturation. A desktop fix should allow concurrent tasks and chat switching without terminating the main process or active work.

Raw dumps and logs remain local because they may contain private content. This public-safe report contains aggregate measurements, release information and code locations, without account IDs, usernames, task IDs, business/project names, local paths or private conversation text.

items.title: Windows desktop: intermittent workspace-settings failures plus missing rollout files after reinstall

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: session
labels.description: Issues involving session (thread) management, resuming, forking, naming, archiving

labels.name: config
labels.description: Issues involving config.toml, config keys, config merging, or config updates

items.body:
## Summary

I am seeing multiple intermittent reliability problems in the Windows desktop app. The two most serious are:

1. **Intermittent `Unable to load workspace settings`** in Codex/Work.
2. **Local conversation persistence failures** where the UI still lists a conversation, but the referenced `.codex\sessions\...\rollout-*.jsonl` file no longer exists.

I am reporting these together because they occurred in the same Windows desktop environment, but I do **not** want to assume they have the same root cause.

The workspace-settings failure reproduced again **after a full uninstall/reinstall with a brand-new `.codex` directory and without restoring any old backup**, so old local state is not sufficient to explain that symptom.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 10, build 10.0.19045.x
- Windows sandbox: `elevated`
- Current app/runtime configuration exposes `BROWSER_USE_CODEX_APP_VERSION = 26.1007.71326`
- Current command runner: `codex-command-runner-0.162.0-alpha.17.2.exe`
- Current `.codex` was created fresh after reinstall
- Old `.codex` was renamed and kept separately; no old backup was restored into the new installation

## 1. Intermittent workspace-settings failure

The UI intermittently shows:

> Unable to load workspace settings
> Please retry to continue chatting

Behavior:

- Highly intermittent.
- Sometimes the app works normally for days.
- When the failure occurs, repeated restarts may or may not recover it.
- On the latest reinstall, the failure returned even with a fresh `.codex`.
- The Retry button sometimes appears to have no effect.
- Restarting the app can temporarily restore normal operation.

### Sandbox log during a recent failure window

The sandbox setup showed one non-fatal Windows error 32 warning on the user profile:

```text
failed to grant non-inheriting read-attributes ACE on user profile C:\Users\<USER>:
open ACL target for root-only update:
The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process. (os error 32);
continuing setup
```

But setup then completed successfully:

```text
setup refresh: processed 0 write roots (read roots delegated); errors=[]
setup binary completed
```

and later:

```text
setup refresh: processed 3 write roots (read roots delegated); errors=[]
setup binary completed
```

So this particular `Unable to load workspace settings` occurrence did **not** coincide with the previously reported fatal runtime ACL failure / `helper_unknown_error: setup refresh had errors` / `node_repl.exe` validation failure.

This makes me suspect the workspace-settings failure may be higher-level than sandbox initialization (for example account/settings API, workspace metadata, app-server state, feature/config schema, or connectivity).

## 2. `logs_2.sqlite` warnings during the same period

The relevant time window contained WARN entries but no ERROR-level entries.

Observed warnings included:

```text
ignoring invalid experimental feature enablement keys:
apps_mcp_path_override
```

and repeated:

```text
unknown feature key in config:
code_mode_tool_description_first
```

There was also:

```text
failed to load plugin:
plugin is not installed
plugin="code-review@openai-bundled"
```

and a sequence of connectivity warnings:

```text
stream disconnected - retrying sampling request
sampling_error=request timed out
```

followed eventually by:

```text
falling back to HTTP
```

I do not know whether these warnings are causally related to the workspace-settings UI failure, but they occurred during the same time range.

## 3. Guardian config warning that does not match the on-disk config

Settings -> Config shows a warning similar to:

```text
[features.guardianv2].thread_context is deprecated and ignored
```

with guidance to remove `thread_context` from `[features.guardianv2]`, including profile overrides.

However:

- `C:\Users\<USER>\.codex\config.toml` does not contain `[features.guardianv2]`.
- A full-text search of the fresh `.codex` directory finds no `thread_context` setting.
- Searching for `guardianv2` only hits unrelated plugin temporary resources.

So the UI warning appears to refer to configuration that is not visible in the current on-disk config.

## 4. Conversation rollout files missing while UI entries remain

In the previous installation, multiple conversations remained visible in the UI but could no longer be opened.

Typical error:

```text
failed to resolve rollout path
'C:\Users\<USER>\.codex\sessions\...\rollout-....jsonl':
file does not exist
```

Symptoms:

- Conversation title still appears in the UI.
- Opening it shows a message-load failure.
- The referenced rollout path is explicit.
- The actual `.jsonl` file is absent from disk.
- This affected more than one conversation and more than one date.
- Some remaining `.jsonl` files were `guardian_review` child sessions while the corresponding main rollout was gone.

This looks like a persistence/index integrity problem: the UI/conversation index still references a session artifact that no longer exists.

I have backups of the old `.codex` trees and did not merge them into the fresh installation.

## 5. Other intermittent Windows desktop symptoms observed

These may be unrelated, but I am including them for triage context:

- `Windows setup incomplete / Setup could not be completed` (historical, has not reproduced recently).
- Archive operation failed for an active chat in the old environment.
- Archived Chats page briefly showed `Unable to load archived chats`, then recovered after navigating away/back.
- Settings UI sometimes visibly re-renders/reorders as account/configuration state arrives asynchronously.
- ChatGPT Work / Codex mode switching can visibly change which recent conversations are shown.

## Relationship to existing Windows sandbox issues

I am aware of related Windows sandbox issues such as #51601, #51981, #52897 and the ACL repair change in #51822.

The important distinction in this report is that the **latest workspace-settings failure happened while sandbox setup completed with `errors=[]`**, so I do not think all of these symptoms should automatically be attributed to the known runtime ACL error-32 issue.

## Questions / request for triage

Could you please help confirm:

1. Is intermittent `Unable to load workspace settings` currently a known Windows desktop issue?
2. Are there known failures involving `/settings/user`, workspace metadata, account settings, feature flags, or app-server state that can produce this UI symptom while sandbox setup itself succeeds?
3. Do `apps_mcp_path_override` / `code_mode_tool_description_first` warnings indicate an app/component/config-schema version mismatch?
4. Where can the `guardianv2.thread_context` deprecation warning originate if the setting is absent from the current `.codex` and `config.toml`?
5. Under what circumstances can `.codex\sessions\...\rollout-*.jsonl` files disappear while the conversation UI/index still references them?
6. Is there a supported integrity check or recovery procedure for local session/index state?
7. Is there a preferred Windows diagnostic bundle / log set / Feedback ID workflow that would help investigate both the workspace-settings failure and the rollout persistence issue?

## Data preserved

I have preserved:

- a pre-reinstall `.codex` backup,
- an older `.codex` backup from a previous reinstall,
- the fresh post-reinstall `.codex`,
- `.sandbox` logs,
- `logs_2.sqlite`,
- screenshots of the UI failures,
- exact missing rollout paths and timestamps.

I have **not** manually modified ACLs, replaced runtime/helper binaries, downgraded sandbox isolation, or copied old `.codex` state back into the fresh installation.

items.title: [Windows][Codex App] Add Pause and Cancel controls to the existing update download progress indicator

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

ChatGPT Desktop / Codex App for Windows OpenAI.Codex MSIX package: 26.1007.2314.0 About ChatGPT (Powered by Codex & OWL): 26.1007.21434

### What feature would you like to see?

## Problem

The ChatGPT/Codex desktop app on Windows does not expose a visible Pause or Cancel control while downloading an application update.

This is especially problematic for users with limited mobile data, metered connections, unstable networks, or shared bandwidth.

Users should not have to disconnect from the internet, terminate the application, or navigate an external update manager just to stop an ongoing download.


## Proposed solution

The Windows desktop app already displays update download progress through a circular indicator and a percentage tooltip (e.g., "Downloading 38%").

However, no Pause or Cancel control is visible in the observed download UI.

Please add:

1. **Pause** — temporarily suspend an ongoing update download.
2. **Resume** — continue a paused download without restarting it from zero, where supported.
3. **Cancel** — stop an ongoing download and prevent that attempt from automatically restarting.
4. **Metered connection support** — respect Windows metered-network preferences or ask for confirmation before downloading large updates.
5. **Update preferences** — let users choose whether updates download automatically or only after confirmation.

The existing progress indicator could provide a contextual menu or expand into a small download-management panel.

Cancelling an update should not terminate the application or interrupt active Codex tasks.

## Expected behavior

When an update is downloading, the user can pause or cancel it without closing the application or interrupting active Codex tasks.

A cancelled update should not silently restart downloading without the user's consent.

The feature should distinguish between checking for updates, downloading an update, and installing an update.


### Additional information


## Environment

- Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC 21H2, x64
- OpenAI.Codex package version: 26.1007.2314.0
- About ChatGPT version: 26.1007.21434

## Related issues

- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/52049 — requests temporarily pausing future updates and supporting rollback, rather than controlling an active download.
- https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/18546 — previous macOS request to disable automatic app updates.

This request specifically concerns user control over an update download that is already in progress on Windows.

items.body:
## Environment

macOS desktop, build 20156, build commit `a993bdbe5bb9503cb84de1e67d5635cf186a959f`. Observed 14 October 2026. Local registered Codex tasks.

This report is sanitized: no private task transcripts, task IDs, account identifiers, credentials or project content.

## Reproduction

1. Choose an existing accessible local Codex task.
2. Call `codex_app.wait_threads` with:

```json
{"targets":[{"hostId":"local","threadId":"<existing-task-id>"}],"timeoutMs":0}
```

3. Call `codex_app.read_thread` for the same ID and host with `turnLimit: 1`, `includeOutputs: false`, and `maxOutputCharsPerItem: 1`.

## Expected

`wait_threads` returns its documented immediate snapshot for `timeoutMs: 0`.

## Actual

`wait_threads` returns `isError: true` with:

```text
tool call error: tool call failed for `codex_app/wait_threads`

Caused by:
    Mcp error: -32000: MCP error -32000: Codex app tool request failed
```

The exact `read_thread` succeeds and returns `schemaVersion: 1`, the correct ID/host and status `idle`.

Reproduced on two distinct tasks. Omitting optional `hostId` did not repair `wait_threads` on the second task. Three earlier attempts against one task failed identically. Direct tool reproduction excludes our sender's response validator as the cause.

## Sanitized desktop log evidence

```text
dynamic_app_tool_renderer_execution_started tool=wait_threads
dynamic_app_tools_request_failed
errorMessage="The app tool call ended before producing a result"
method=tools/call

Comparison:
response_routed method=thread/read errorCode=null
Sending server response success=true tool=read_thread
```

Logs show the same wait call dispatched to multiple renderer windows (primary windows and avatar overlay). This is an observation, **not a proven cause**. No underlying exception identifying the wait-handler defect was exposed.

## Impact and workaround

A workflow needing only an exact task status exhausts bounded preparation retries and falls back to manual notification, without sending native activation.

We have switched that status check to the supported exact `read_thread` tool, retaining identity, freshness and duplicate protections. Successful natural delivery with this workaround is not yet established. The workaround does not require a permission bypass.

Please investigate the `wait_threads` renderer dispatch/result-completion path, especially `timeoutMs: 0`, and return a useful structured failure if execution cannot produce a snapshot.

items.body:
## App version
Installed macOS desktop app is branded ChatGPT, with a Codex work surface (composer says "Work with Codex"). Bundle version: 26.1007.71326, build 20398. Reporting here under the Codex App template; please redirect if this surface belongs to a different tracker.

## Subscription
Paid ChatGPT subscription, reported by user as approximately US$200/month; exact plan label not independently checked.

## Platform
`Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 arm`

## Issue
Follow-up messages remain displayed in a pending queue with spinners after an assistant response visibly finishes. The queue grew from one to five and then seven messages. During the stuck state there was no visible Stop button or Steer control. The user reports the condition persisted for approximately 30 minutes and restarting the app at least three times over four hours did not resolve the recurring problem.

Some messages shown as pending were already present in the assistant's conversation context and had received replies. Identical message text subsequently appeared again as separate user messages and received additional replies. This establishes a visible delivery/display mismatch, but does not establish whether the underlying cause is resubmission, queue replay, rendering, acknowledgement handling, or another synchronization issue.

Later, the UI showed Thinking and a Stop button again, and Steer controls reappeared beside most queued messages. One pending item still showed a spinner. This was intermittent recovery of controls, not verified recovery of the queue.

## Observed steps (not a clean minimal reproduction)
1. Use an existing long-running Codex desktop conversation for browser-assisted work.
2. Send follow-up instructions/comments while work is ongoing or as a response completes.
3. Observe a completed assistant reply with copy/feedback controls while follow-ups remain in a queue showing spinners and delete icons.
4. Send further messages attempting to redirect the conversation; queue entries accumulate and Steer is unavailable in the observed idle-looking state.
5. Observe repeated message text in the conversation, including content still shown as pending on the user's screen.
6. Eventually Thinking/Stop/Steer reappear without a confirmed fix.

## Expected behavior
After completion, pending messages should be processed or show a clear actionable error. An active turn should expose applicable steering controls consistently. Delivered/answered messages should not remain ambiguously pending, and messages should not be replayed as new actions. The displayed queue and conversation delivery state should agree.

## Timing and configuration
Observed on 14 October 2026, approximately 13:06-13:23 SAST (UTC+2), with the user reporting a longer roughly 30-minute stall. The visible non-secret preference was `[desktop] followUpQueueMode = "queue"`. Queue mode may explain why follow-ups wait during active work, but not the prolonged post-response pending display or repeated messages. No causal claim about this setting is made.

## Impact
Unable to reliably steer ongoing work or determine whether a prompt has been delivered. Repeated consequential instructions could cause duplicate actions; in this incident the assistant treated obvious repeats as duplicates.

## Related reports
Search found #50395 (similar symptoms in VS Code) and #48928 / #51625 (external steering interface requests). This report concerns the macOS desktop UI's pending/display/repeated-message behavior, not a request for a CLI steering API.

## Privacy and evidence
Screenshots were reviewed locally. No unredacted screenshots, sensitive task contents, full configuration, credentials, or private conversation identifiers are included in this public report. No backend logs or root-cause diagnosis have been obtained. Public text is a sanitized account of observed UI behavior and user-reported duration/restart attempts.

items.title: CLI: same-host --remote unix:// silently uses daemon cwd unless --cd is supplied

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

items.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

codex-cli 0.162.1; managed app-server 0.162.1.

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro.

### Which model were you using?

GPT-6.1-Sol was selected, but reproduction requires no model request.

### What platform is your computer?

Ubuntu Linux, x86_64.

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

Initially noticed in Herdr 0.8.2. Independently reproduced using the native standalone Codex binary in a separate PTY, with HERDR_* caller context removed and no shell wrapper.

### Codex doctor report

Native diagnostics confirmed CLI and managed server both use 0.162.1, the daemon is running, config parses, and state databases pass integrity checks. Full report omitted because it contains unrelated local workspace metadata.

### What issue are you seeing?

Connecting to the same machine's managed daemon using `codex --remote unix://` silently changes the new session's working directory from the terminal's project directory to the daemon's directory (home in this reproduction).

This affected a workflow where terminal and phone attach to the same app-server. The client process had the correct launch cwd, but the resulting session used home. Explicit `--cd` fixes it.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Have the managed daemon running from a different directory, for example home (`codex remote-control start`). Do not stop or restart a daemon serving active work just to reproduce this.
2. Create an empty synthetic directory and launch the native binary directly:

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/codex-cwd-repro/project
cd /tmp/codex-cwd-repro/project
command codex --remote unix:// --no-alt-screen
```

3. Run the local `/status` command. Observed: `Directory: ~` and the existing managed Unix control socket as `Server`. No task prompt was submitted.
4. Exit that empty TUI and run the control:

```bash
command codex --remote unix:// --cd "$PWD" --no-alt-screen
```

Observed: the new session shows `/tmp/codex-cwd-repro/project` as its directory.

### What is the expected behavior?

For the canonical same-host managed daemon endpoint, preserve the terminal's launch directory, or make the requirement for explicit `--cd` clearly visible before a new task starts in a different directory.

I understand that a genuinely remote workspace may intentionally default to the server directory. This report concerns the surprising same-host managed-daemon case; it is not a request to blindly forward local paths to every WebSocket or forwarded Unix endpoint.

### Additional information

Source inspection at commit `78dc2503840d05f4411ae184bb5560ef327fce3c` suggests why:

- [`AppServerTarget::uses_remote_workspace`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/78dc2503840d05f4411ae184bb5560ef327fce3c/codex-rs/tui/src/lib.rs#L342) returns true for `Remote` regardless of the Unix transport.
- [`config_cwd_for_app_server_target`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/78dc2503840d05f4411ae184bb5560ef327fce3c/codex-rs/tui/src/lib.rs#L919) returns no local cwd for that target.
- The nearby `config_cwd_for_app_server_target_omits_cwd_for_remote_sessions` test explicitly covers a Unix socket. This may therefore be intentional remote semantics with a missing distinction or diagnostic for the canonical local-daemon attachment, rather than a simple cwd propagation omission.

A possible direction is to retain local-daemon semantics when explicitly attaching to the canonical same-host control endpoint, or warn/document that `--remote unix://` requires `--cd` to retain launch cwd. Preserve truly remote filesystem semantics and explicit `--cd` choices.

Related but different: #31317 concerns the resume picker's cwd filter despite explicit `--cd`; #42457 concerns hook cwd; #46145 concerns workspace roots despite a correct explicit cwd. Here, the new session's directory itself changes when `--cd` is omitted.

Local workaround: pass `--cd "$PWD"` when launching the interactive client against the shared local server. No private project names, conversation content, account identifiers, or real session IDs are included here.

items.title: Voice dictation: resolve spoken skill names into explicit skill invocations

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: skills
labels.description: Issues related to skills

items.body:
### What feature would you like to see?

In Codex Desktop, let users explicitly invoke an installed skill by saying its name during voice dictation. Resolve an intentional spoken invocation into the same native skill reference/mention that the composer produces when the user manually selects a skill with `$skill-name`.

### Problem

I use voice dictation and have skills configured to require explicit invocation (`allow_implicit_invocation: false`). Saying a skill's name does not reliably produce the explicit reference I would insert with the keyboard. Speech recognition can also change an English skill name into ordinary words or a phonetic transcription.

I have to interrupt dictation, type `$`, and select the skill manually. This makes a voice-first workflow cumbersome. I encounter the same need in the ChatGPT desktop app; this request focuses on Codex Desktop.

### Example

Assume an installed skill named `code-review` (an illustrative name).

I dictate:

> Use code-review and check the changes.

Expected: the composer recognizes the deliberate request to use that installed skill and inserts the native explicit reference equivalent to manually selecting `$code-review`, while preserving the rest of the dictated text.

The user should not have to pronounce punctuation or switch to the keyboard to get explicit invocation semantics.

### Desired behavior

- Use the names of skills available in the current session as recognition/resolution context.
- Support mixed-language dictation, especially Russian speech containing English skill names, including hyphenated names.
- Resolve an intentional invocation to the actual installed skill identity, rather than merely inserting similar-looking plain text.
- Preserve explicit-only semantics: a deliberate spoken invocation should work for a skill with implicit invocation disabled, without enabling implicit invocation generally.
- Show the resolved skill reference in the composer before submission, with the ability to remove or correct it.
- For ambiguous names or low-confidence recognition, offer a choice or leave the transcript editable instead of silently selecting a skill.
- Distinguish an invocation such as “use the code-review skill” from merely discussing that skill; mentioning a name in passing should not activate it.

### Why this is useful

This would make explicit skill selection practical during voice input and reduce manual corrections of technical identifiers. It would also let users keep control over which skills run while working primarily by voice.

### Related issues

- #44486 — Mark dictated messages so Codex can account for transcription errors. Related dictation context; this request specifically concerns resolving a spoken skill name into an explicit skill invocation.
- #38504 — Live Voice as a first-class Codex orchestration surface. Broader live-voice workflow; this request is a focused improvement to dictation in the composer.
- #40874 — Global explicit-only mode for skills. Related invocation policy; this request provides a voice equivalent of explicit manual selection.
