items.title: Repeated suspected cybersecurity false positives interrupt local code audits and unittest maintenance (CLI 0.162.1)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: safety-check
labels.description: Issues related to safety and abuse checks

items.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

`codex-cli 0.162.1`, verified locally on October 14, 2026.

### What subscription do you have?

Not independently verified for this report.

### Which model were you using?

An earlier affected CLI transcript reports GPT-6.1-Sol with reasoning effort `max`. The exact model and reasoning level of the most recent blocked turn were not captured independently.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS; verified `uname -mprs`: `Darwin 20.6.0 x86_64 i386`.

### What terminal emulator and version are you using?

Codex CLI TUI. Terminal emulator/version not independently captured.

### Codex doctor report

Not attached: this public report is deliberately limited to the incident and feedback references, rather than local paths, configuration and state inventories.

### What issue are you seeing?

I repeatedly receive the following notice while working on code that I own and am authorized to test:

> This content can’t be shown

The rest of the notice refers to extra care with cybersecurity requests and links to:
- https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001326
- https://openai.com/form/enterprise-trusted-access-for-cyber/

After the notice, the CLI returns to the input prompt and the ongoing task stops. Asking to continue has also encountered the same notice in earlier episodes.

The work includes defensive review of my own application in an isolated test environment, and ordinary Python maintenance of my local task/audit tooling and unittest cases. The recent tooling work records the start and outcome of a test, preserves unfinished steps after interruption, and protects checkpoint data. It does not involve third-party scanning, credential theft, production attacks, or exploit deployment.

I suspect a false positive, but I cannot establish the classifier trigger or prove misclassification from the banner alone. Please investigate rather than treating this report as a request to bypass safeguards.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

The sequence below is observed in my supplied transcript; it is not a deterministic minimal reproducer:

1. Authorize work on my own code and synthetic local test fixtures.
2. Let Codex inspect the local code and prepare regression tests.
3. A local pre-edit policy check for an 806-line unittest candidate returns `PASS`.
4. The cybersecurity notice appears and the task returns to the input prompt.

At that particular notice, the new test candidate had **not been applied**, and **zero new journal tests had run**. Therefore, the last visible successful command is only a timing reference, not evidence that this command caused the classification.

Subsequent permitted local work completed the checkpoint change. Its eight new regressions passed, and an independent compatibility check passed 21 registry tests and 50 defensive-workflow tests with synthetic fixtures. These later results support the benign context of the tooling work; they do not identify the earlier classifier trigger.

### What is the expected behavior?

Authorized ordinary code maintenance and defensive testing should proceed reliably within the supported policy and execution boundaries.

If a particular step is restricted, please provide actionable information about that step and a supported way to resume the remaining permitted work. Preserve the current task, completed results and checkpoint state, and distinguish a service content restriction from a local tool failure. Do not silently imply that the task completed when the turn was interrupted.

These repeated interruptions have materially delayed my project work over multiple days, consumed time and usage, and forced manual restarts and context recovery.

### Additional information

Official Codex `feedback/upload` acknowledged reports associated with this primary thread:

`01a12576-0fa5-7ca3-b3cc-7504ad26ecfa`

A separate affected CLI transcript also reports an uploaded thread:

`01a13776-4a2a-7a13-8b1f-15d81bad033a`

The primary-thread uploads were made with `includeLogs=false` and `extraLogFiles=[]`. Their returned `promptHash` was identical across uploads, so I do not treat it as a unique support ticket or a resolution. The separate transcript’s upload has not been independently verified in this report.

The precise timestamp and request ID for the latest banner were not supplied. Report date: October 14, 2026; my working timezone is Europe/Moscow (UTC+03:00).

No private source code, full prompts/conversations, credentials, server endpoints or raw security logs are attached. Related public reports found before filing: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/53144 and https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/44614 . This report supplies my own affected threads and a recent ordinary unittest/checkpoint-maintenance episode.

items.title: Codex CLI 0.162.1 remains Working for 16+ minutes after completion update, with output usage but no delivered action

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

items.body:
## What issue are you seeing?

Codex CLI remained in a running turn without delivering the requested document after announcing that its research reports and verification were complete. The terminal continued showing "Working"; the user's screenshot showed an elapsed time of 22m 10s. There was no visible explanation of a blocker or of the prolonged generation.

The inspected session transcript records no tool call after 08:16:23.542 UTC. It subsequently records 8,498 output tokens for a model response, but no corresponding completed assistant message or tool call was present in the inspected interval. After a user steering message was recorded, the session still did not record a further tool action or turn completion through 08:32:57.668 UTC.

This is an observed incident, not a confirmed diagnosis. The transcript does not establish whether the cause was slow generation, an interrupted/discarded generation, stream handling, or a CLI issue.

## Environment

- Component: Codex CLI terminal UI.
- CLI version: 0.162.1, confirmed by both session metadata and `codex --version`.
- Platform: Linux; shell: zsh.
- Model: `gpt-6.1-sol`.
- Reasoning effort: `high`.
- Session metadata: originator `codex-tui`, source `vscode`, provider `openai`.
- Incident date: October 14, 2026.
- Session ID: `01a13976-25e9-7a81-8b72-57021b32bc30`.
- Subscription tier: not verified.

## Observed sequence

Times below are UTC; the terminal user's local time was UTC+02:00.

| Time | Recorded event |
| --- | --- |
| 08:11:06.467 | Task started. |
| 08:16:23.542 | Last recorded tool call. Its output returned successfully at 08:16:23.594. |
| 08:16:31.014 | Assistant announced that all seven reports were complete and said what the requested document would include. |
| 08:23:18.721 | Token-count event; no intervening completed tool call or assistant deliverable recorded. |
| 08:27:23.703 | Usage record: input_tokens=150842, cached_input_tokens=150528, output_tokens=8498, reasoning_output_tokens=0, total_tokens=159340. |
| 08:27:23.709 | User steering message recorded, explicitly instructing Codex to write the document immediately. |
| 08:27:28.776 | Reasoning response item recorded. |
| 08:32:57.668 | Token-count event; still no further completed tool action or turn completion recorded in the inspected transcript. |

The gap from the completion update to the last inspected event is approximately 16 minutes 27 seconds. The usage entry is evidence of reported generation, not proof that useful work was delivered.

## Steps leading to the incident

1. Ask Codex to prepare a repository context document using several research reports.
2. Let it complete the reports and its verification.
3. Observe its progress message announcing that all seven reports are complete.
4. Wait for the final document to be saved.
5. While the turn remains running, send a steering message telling it to write the document immediately.
6. Observe the continuing "Working" indicator without a delivered document, further tool action, or actionable error during the inspected interval.

A deterministic reproduction from a fresh session has not been established.

## Expected behavior

Codex should save and return the requested document promptly after completing the necessary research, or explain the actual blocker. If a generation or stream stalls, the CLI should expose an actionable status, timeout, or retry path rather than leaving a running indicator with no useful progress for many minutes.

## Impact and evidence handling

The user cannot tell whether work is progressing or whether it is safe to interrupt. Reported output usage without a corresponding deliverable also makes the delay difficult to diagnose.

This report contains selected event metadata only. Repository code, database query results, credentials, full transcripts, and the original screenshot are omitted.

- Native `wss://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses`; model `gpt-6.1-sol`; Responses Lite; `reasoning.context="all_turns"`. Probes used the system-configured HTTP CONNECT proxy with TLS certificate verification enabled.
- Selected Ultra resolves to wire `xhigh` through the model's supported `multi_agent_reasoning_effort`: [official resolver](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.162.1/codex-rs/protocol/src/openai_models/reasoning_effort.rs).
- Configured window: 500,000; usable window: 475,000; auto-compaction threshold: 450,000; scope: `total`.

## What issue are you seeing?

The desktop showed **54% used, approximately 255k / 475k**, while automatic compaction started. Matching local counters reconcile exactly:

```json
{
  "last_api_total_tokens": 255367,
  "historical_encrypted_reasoning_items": 193,
  "client_historical_reasoning_estimate": 200147,
  "new_local_tail_estimate": 0,
  "client_compaction_counter": 455514,
  "auto_compact_threshold": 450000,
  "usable_window": 475000,
  "ui_percent_used": 54
}
```

`255367 + 200147 + 0 = 455514 > 450000`.

The installed estimator is `ceil(max(floor(3 * encoded_length / 4) - 650, 0) / 4)`. Summing the selected 193 historical items reproduces 200,147 exactly. An earlier boundary also reconciles: `250351 + 191197 = 441548` for 185 items.

The installed binary's calculation was checked separately; the public release source below is supporting correspondence, not assumed identical to the private desktop build.

### Completed-generation confirmation

Two bounded **actual generation requests** used the same authenticated native route, model, Lite profile, `all_turns`, wire `xhigh`, and one connection.

The second request added exactly one compatible old encrypted reasoning item before the latest user message: 3,108 encoded characters, no plaintext reasoning, client estimate 421. Removing that item produced a normalized request hash identical to the baseline. No `previous_response_id` was sent.

```json
{
  "max_output_tokens_requested_and_echoed": 128,
  "baseline": {
    "status": "completed",
    "input_tokens": 27,
    "output_tokens": 33,
    "total_tokens": 60
  },
  "with_old_reasoning": {
    "status": "completed",
    "input_tokens": 143,
    "output_tokens": 25,
    "total_tokens": 168
  },
  "input_delta": 116,
  "client_estimate_of_the_added_item": 421,
  "upgrade_x_reasoning_included_present": false,
  "all_observed_metadata_x_reasoning_included_present": false
}
```

Both responses echoed the expected model and `all_turns`. Total generated output was 58 tokens, within the requested caps. The HTTP 101 upgrade and every observed `codex.response.metadata.headers` object lacked `x-reasoning-included`.

The 116-token input increase is attributable to the old item and associated framing, already included in reported input usage. Applying the installed missing-signal fallback additionally estimates that same item as 421, making the inclusive 168 total **589**. This proves overlapping accounting on the tested generation route; 421 is not its actual model-token count.

## Steps to reproduce

1. On the same native ChatGPT-backed model/Lite/`all_turns` route, retain one compatible encrypted reasoning item from an earlier successful response.
2. Send a baseline `response.create` request with `store=false`, `stream=true`, `include=["reasoning.encrypted_content"]`, `reasoning={"effort":"xhigh","context":"all_turns"}`, and `max_output_tokens=128`. Use the native Lite headers (`OpenAI-Beta: responses_websockets=2026-02-06`, `x-openai-internal-codex-responses-lite: true`) and its client-metadata mirror. The input messages are user **"Acknowledge with OK."**, assistant **"OK"**, then user **"Repeat that acknowledgement."**
3. On the same connection, send the identical full request with only that old reasoning item inserted after the first user and before the assistant message. Do not feed the first request's output into the second.
4. Compare completed input usage and inspect upgrade/metadata headers for `x-reasoning-included`.
5. Reconcile the missing-signal client calculation using the encoded-length estimator.

These steps need no private conversation text or publicly shared encrypted payload.

## Expected behavior

When usage already includes historical reasoning, compaction should use it plus genuinely new local items, without adding the historical estimate again. Bind the inclusion contract to its successful usage through the next pre-turn check and resume/fork. The UI should expose the actual compaction counter and threshold.

The official [history counter](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.162.1/codex-rs/core/src/context_manager/history.rs) adds historical estimates when the flag is false; the [WebSocket handler](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.162.1/codex-rs/codex-api/src/endpoint/responses_websocket.rs) reads the upgrade header. The [request builder](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.162.1/codex-rs/core/src/client.rs) selects `all_turns` for Lite.

## Additional information and limits

Related reports: [#53309](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/53309), [#49961](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/49961). This adds independent exact arithmetic and completed-generation evidence.

Original incident headers were not retained. The reproduction cannot locate an origin/edge/forwarding-layer omission or recover the true server token count of all 193 items. The probe User-Agent was not confirmed identical to the historical connection.

A scoped candidate against official `rust-v0.162.1` is **STATIC_ONLY**: source review, `git apply --check`, and `rustfmt --check` completed. It has **not been compiled, Rust tests have not been executed, it has not been installed, and patch runtime behavior is unverified**. It covers live sampling/local-compaction pairing; **resume/fork contract persistence is not implemented**. No deployed fix or update-resolution claim is made.

Please confirm and repair the native Lite usage/inclusion-signal contract and its client lifecycle. Raising the compaction threshold leaves overlapping accounting intact.

items.title: Massive `git` zombie process leak when a mobile Remote Control client attaches to a running session (per-file `git diff --no-index` children are never reaped)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

items.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

codex-cli 0.162.1 (x86_64-unknown-linux-musl) Also reproduced on 0.159.2 (npm install) earlier the same day.

### What subscription do you have?

chatgpt pro

### Which model were you using?

6.1-sol

### What platform is your computer?

x86_64 GNU/Linux

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

Not applicable — the leak occurs in the headless codex app-server (remote-control daemon / SSH-launched) on a Linux server, not in an interactive terminal. No multiplexer involved.

### Codex doctor report

```json
not available
```

### What issue are you seeing?

On a shared Linux dev server (Ubuntu, ~500 GiB RAM), attaching a mobile Remote Control client to a running Codex session triggers an unbounded background diff enumeration over the repo's untracked files: Codex spawns one `git diff --no-index /dev/null <file>` per untracked file (with --binary), and the children are never reaped.

Observed on codex-cli 0.162.1:

- ~10-16 git processes spawned per second, sustained for hours
- Up to ~15,000 git children simultaneously ALIVE, stuck in `pipe_write` (diff output saturates the stdout pipe and the consumer stops reading)
- Tens of thousands of DEAD children accumulate as zombies (Z state) under a single codex parent: 73,994 zombies in the first storm, 67,099 in a second storm the same afternoon; an earlier incident reached ~84,700 simultaneous git processes (298,955 total created) under one parent PID
- Zombies hold no user-space RSS but permanently occupy PID slots and non-swappable kernel memory. At the observed rate the server (pid_max=4194304, shared by the whole team) was ~2.5 days from fork() exhaustion for ALL users

Live sample captured in the storm (stuck in pipe_write):

    git -c safe.bareRepository=explicit \
        -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null \
        -c core.fsmonitor=false \
        diff --no-textconv --no-ext-diff --binary --no-index \
        -- /dev/null <untracked file>

A minimal control experiment with the same argv confirms the mechanism: with the read end held open and unread, git blocks in pipe_write; closing the read end makes it exit via SIGPIPE; continuously reading completes in ~10 ms.

Key behaviors:

1. Disconnecting the mobile client does NOT stop the leak - new git creation continues until the parent task process exits. Even issuing `codex app-server daemon disable-remote-control` (confirmed remoteControlEnabled=false + shutdown_requested) did not stop the running task chain for several minutes.
2. Killing the parent process is the only effective workaround - when it exited, all ~74k zombies were reaped by init instantly.
3. Disabling Remote Control does not remediate an affected session - after disabling it, the same session/workspace accessed again via a desktop SSH app-server produced the second storm (~67k zombies).
4. Total zombies far exceeded the untracked-file count (73,994 vs ~20,000), indicating the per-file diff enumeration was re-submitted multiple times (workspace refreshes / client reconnects appear to re-trigger full passes) rather than being deduplicated.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Observed sequence on the server:

1. Repo with a large number of UNTRACKED files (20,000+ at incident time; ~10,000 after cleanup) - generated artifacts, datasets, large binary data files, third-party source copies.
2. Desktop app attaches via SSH; a Codex task runs normally in this workspace (no anomaly).
3. A mobile client attaches to the SAME running session via Remote Control -> within minutes the server starts spawning git at ~10-16/sec; memory and zombie count climb.
4. Mobile client disconnects -> the leak does NOT stop.
5. Observe:

    ps -e -o stat= | grep -c Z          # grows ~10-16/sec, reaches tens of thousands
    ps -e -o stat=,comm= | grep ^Z      # all zombies are git
    ps -e -o ppid=,stat= | grep Z       # all share one parent: the codex task/app-server process

Parent-child chain:

    codex app-server (launched either as
      `codex app-server --remote-control --listen unix:// --managed-daemon`
      or by a desktop app SSH connection)
      +- codex task process (code-mode host)
           +- tens of thousands of git children, dying and never reaped

### What is the expected behavior?

1. Background diff enumeration must have a bounded queue / concurrency limit and a total output cap.
2. Diff generation should skip or batch-handle large untracked sets (respect ignore rules, cap file size/count) instead of one `git diff --no-index` per file.
3. Client disconnect / cancel must propagate to the task: stop spawning, drain or close pipes, terminate or wait children.
4. Repeated workspace refreshes / reconnects must not re-submit a full enumeration pass without deduplication.
5. Every spawned child must be reaped regardless of the pipe/cancel path (kill-on-drop must not drop the waiter task).

### Additional information

Related issues:
- #32219 (closed as completed 2026-08-07) - PTY/pipe child-process reaping. The fix appears to cover the PTY ProcessHandle path, but this leak reproduces on 0.162.1 via a different path: the per-file `git diff --no-index` background diff generation.
- #12491 - MCP child processes not reaped (1,300+ zombies) - same symptom family.
- #25744 - desktop app accumulating 126+ zombies; killing children only increases the count, only parent restart clears.

Workarounds we use:
1. Kill the leaking codex task process - zombies are reaped instantly by init; the session JSONL on disk survives and can be resumed.
2. Add generated-artifact directories to .gitignore so the untracked-file enumeration never sees them.
3. Never attach a second client (mobile remote) to a session whose task is running.
4. Monitor: watch -n 30 'ps -e -o stat= | grep -c Z' - if it passes ~50k, kill the task process.

Happy to provide additional evidence: process-tree snapshots with full argv, /proc/<pid>/stack showing pipe_write, timeline logs, and a quantified incident report.

## Summary
On native Windows, Codex desktop Computer Use fails during initialization, before app/window enumeration or any mouse/keyboard input. Ordinary PowerShell commands and Blender background file loading still work. This blocks basic desktop-operation validation and an architectural drawing-underlay workflow.

Related: #48443. This report adds a native-Windows Computer Use case; it does not establish that both reports have the same root cause.

## Environment
- Observed: 2026-10-14, approximately 15:03–16:51 JST (UTC+09:00).
- Native Windows / PowerShell; workspace-write with a managed restricted filesystem permission profile.
- OpenAI Computer Use plugin version: 26.1007.71326.
- Exact Codex desktop app version and Windows build: not captured in this report.
- Target applications: Blender 5.2.0 LTS and SketchUp Desktop 2026, version 26.2.243.
- Four-monitor/RDP/capture setup reported by the user. No evidence currently establishes that this causes the initialization failure.

## Steps observed
1. In the local desktop task, initialize the supported Computer Use runtime (@oai/sky) in a fresh session.
2. Initialization terminates with the errors below, before list_apps/list_windows can be reached.
3. Consequently, selection, orbit/pan/zoom, simple drawing, and Undo cannot be tested through this input path.

## Actual result
```text
node_repl kernel exited unexpectedly
failed to prepare MXC sandbox: permission path cannot be represented losslessly
```

Separate official screenshot observations succeeded. In one observation an untitled SketchUp 2026 window was visibly present on DISPLAY2, while the screenshot window/focus summary reported no active window/no windows. This discrepancy is a separate observation, not proof of the cause of the MXC error.

No successful mouse/keyboard input or completed basic GUI test is claimed.

## Expected result
Computer Use should initialize with supported filesystem permissions, enumerate the actual windows, and allow a bounded basic-operation test. If a permission entry is unsupported, the diagnostic should identify the relevant entry safely and explain a supported recovery procedure, rather than terminating the helper with a generic path-serialization error.

## Diagnostics and limits
- Ordinary local shell read/write checks worked.
- Blender background loading of an existing saved model completed successfully; its source file remained unchanged. This does not prove live GUI operation.
- A drive-root writable permission (E:\\) was present. Other reports suggested drive-root entries as a possible trigger.
- With user authorization and a verified backup, only that E:\\ entry was removed from config.toml; TOML parsing and equality of all other settings were checked.
- A subsequent operator turn still exposed E:\\ in its effective permission profile. Therefore a changed-permission runtime test has NOT occurred, and removal is NOT a confirmed workaround. Application restart/configuration reload is pending confirmation.
- No target-app reinstall, permission bypass, repeated unchanged initialization attempts, or destructive cleanup was used to claim recovery.
- The failing internal permission entry has not been identified.

## Impact / request
Basic desktop automation is unusable in this environment at present, although background processing remains available. Please investigate MXC permission-path serialization and how desktop tasks refresh the effective permission profile after a config change. A safe diagnostic exposing the failing entry index and normalization/round-trip stage would help.

This is a sanitized report submitted at the user's request. It intentionally excludes account identifiers, local usernames, full configuration files, session transcripts, desktop screenshots, and project drawings.

items.title: env::var().ok() swallows non-UTF-8 values across auth and config paths — doctor certifies auth the runtime then can't read

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: auth
labels.description: Issues related to authentication and accounts

labels.name: CLI
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex CLI

labels.name: config
labels.description: Issues involving config.toml, config keys, config merging, or config updates

items.body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

codex-cli 0.162.1 (release binary; source read at main, cloned 2026-10-14)

### What subscription do you have?

N/A — no account interaction involved; env/auth resolution layer, reproduced locally from the release binary

### Which model were you using?

N/A — the env/auth resolution layer runs before any model call

### What platform is your computer?

Darwin 23.6.0 arm64 arm

### What terminal emulator and version are you using (if applicable)?

N/A — non-interactive codex doctor

### Codex doctor report

```json
Excerpt (the relevant check, from `CODEX_API_KEY=$'\xff\xfe' codex doctor`):

  ✓ auth         auth is provided by environment
      auth storage mode        File
      auth.json path (file backend/fallback) /private/tmp/codex-probe-home/auth.json
      auth env vars present    CODEX_API_KEY

With no stored credentials, the same environment then fails auth resolution as if the variable were unset — the two components read the same variable with different APIs (details in the issue body).
```

### What issue are you seeing?

Same bug family as #48124 (which I verified is still present on `main`), but the pattern is repo-wide: `std::env::var(..).ok()` maps `VarError::NotUnicode` to `None`, making a set-but-non-UTF-8 value indistinguishable from absent. Production instances (all at `main`):

| site | reads | effect of a non-UTF-8 value |
|---|---|---|
| `login/src/auth/manager.rs:958` `read_openai_api_key_from_env` | `OPENAI_API_KEY` | key treated as absent |
| `login/src/auth/manager.rs:963-970` `read_non_empty_env_var` | `CODEX_API_KEY`, `CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN` | **top-precedence auth method silently skipped** (`manager.rs:1503`: "API key via env var takes precedence over any other auth method") |
| `model-provider-info/src/lib.rs:483` `ModelProviderInfo::api_key` | provider `env_key` | `EnvVarError` "not found" — misattributes the failure |
| `exec-server/src/environment.rs:680` `optional_environment_value` | session env passthrough | value dropped |
| `utils/home-dir/src/lib.rs:14` | `CODEX_HOME` | #48124 |

The sharp edge is that **doctor checks the same variables with `env::var_os`** (`cli/src/doctor.rs:3048` `env_var_present`), so the two components disagree. Verified on the 0.162.1 release binary:

```
$ CODEX_API_KEY=$'\xff\xfe' codex doctor
  ✓ auth         auth is provided by environment
      auth env vars present    CODEX_API_KEY
```

while the auth resolver (var-based) skips that very value and falls through to "no credentials". Doctor certifies auth the runtime then can't read.

Root-cause note + suggested direction — per-type policy rather than one blanket change:

- **String-valued vars (keys/tokens/URLs)**: these end up in HTTP headers or URLs, so they must be UTF-8; the fix is to surface `NotUnicode` as an explicit error in each reader's existing style ("CODEX_API_KEY is set but not valid UTF-8"), instead of folding it into not-set. A shared helper (e.g. `read_env_var_utf8(name) -> Result<Option<String>, VarError>`) would make the policy uniform and testable.
- **Path-valued vars** (`CODEX_HOME`): `var_os` is correct — `AbsolutePathBuf` already carries a raw `PathBuf` (see #48124 for that analysis).

In-repo precedent for both directions: #15360 (moved PATH to `OsString` for exactly this reason) and `cli/src/doctor/system.rs:35`, where `EDITOR_ENV_VARS` already uses `env::var_os` two lines below a `var().ok()` locale read.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

On macOS/Linux (zsh/bash), with no stored credentials (fresh `CODEX_HOME`, no `auth.json`):

1. `export CODEX_HOME=$(mktemp -d)`
2. `CODEX_API_KEY=$'\xff\xfe' codex doctor` → observe `✓ auth — auth is provided by environment`, `auth env vars present CODEX_API_KEY` (doctor's presence check uses `env::var_os`, which sees the non-UTF-8 value)
3. Run any auth-requiring command in the same environment → auth resolution treats the variable as unset (`read_non_empty_env_var` uses `env::var(..).ok()`, which maps `NotUnicode` → `None`), falling through to "no credentials"

Control: `CODEX_API_KEY=sk-test123 codex doctor` behaves identically on the doctor side, and the runtime path reads the key — only the non-UTF-8 value splits the two components' views.

### What is the expected behavior?

The two components agree on what the environment contains. Either:

- the auth readers surface `NotUnicode` as an explicit error ("CODEX_API_KEY is set but not valid UTF-8 — refusing to silently treat it as unset"), which also makes doctor's ✓ accurate by construction (the failure becomes loud and attributed), or
- if silent tolerance is intended, doctor should report the variable as present-but-unusable rather than endorsing it as working auth.

The per-type policy suggested in the issue body: `var_os` for path-valued variables (already the pattern in-repo), explicit UTF-8 errors for string-valued variables that feed headers/URLs.

### Additional information

Searched the tracker before filing; the only related item is #48124 (CODEX_HOME instance of the same family, still open, with my verification and fix analysis in its thread). Filed as a separate issue because the affected surfaces and the right fix differ per site (paths vs strings). Related prior art in-repo: #15360 (PATH → OsString).

Disclosure: prepared with the help of an AI coding agent. Source lines cited from a fresh clone of `main` (2026-10-14); the doctor output quoted was run locally from the v0.162.1 release binary before filing.

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.1007.30912 (build 20156), bundle identifier `com.openai.codex`.

Version verified from the installed application's Info.plist. Bundled Codex CLI: `0.162.0-alpha.17.2`.

### What subscription do you have?

ChatGPT Pro, using ChatGPT account sign-in.

### What platform is your computer?

```text
Darwin 25.4.0 arm64 arm
```

- macOS 26.4.1 (25E253)
- Apple Silicon MacBook Pro, hardware model `MacBookPro18,1`

### What issue are you seeing?

Opening a new Codex chat displays the localized equivalent of:

> Couldn't load workspace settings  
> Retry to continue chatting

This blocks submitting the first prompt and interrupts normal desktop work.

This is an additional reproduction of the failure reported in #53333 and #52746. The useful distinction in these diagnostics is that **native DeviceCheck attestation generation succeeds in approximately 16–25 ms, but the subsequent registration returns HTTP 403**. Local app-server configuration requests succeed during the same window.

The latest investigated occurrence was on **2026-10-14 around 07:15–07:18 UTC** (15:15–15:18 UTC+8), immediately after a desktop application launch.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

On the affected installation:

1. Launch the desktop application with the existing ChatGPT sign-in.
2. Open a new Codex chat.
3. Observe the workspace-settings warning and inability to submit the first prompt.

No large prompt, image attachment, or long conversation is required for this new-chat failure. A model-specific prompt, context-window utilization, and an established conversation ID are not applicable to this reproduction because it is blocked before the first prompt.

The failure was observed again after the application launched at 07:15:33 UTC. A recovery from the Retry button has not been independently verified in this investigation.

### What is the expected behavior?

With valid account and device verification, a new Codex chat should load its required workspace settings and allow the first prompt to be sent.

If device registration fails, please expose an actionable error and a supported recovery procedure that preserves existing conversations and project settings. The generic workspace-settings warning does not explain the underlying registration failure.

### Additional information

#### Sanitized diagnostic evidence

The following are selected fields from desktop logs, with timestamps in UTC. Account IDs, request IDs, device tokens, cookies, and private paths have been omitted.

```text
2026-10-14T07:15:47.594Z
sa_server_request_failed
routePattern=/settings/user
errorCode=devicecheck_registration_http_failed
errorMessage="DeviceCheck registration failed (403)"
status=500

2026-10-14T07:16:11.398Z
[devicecheck-attestation] DeviceCheck attestation generated
deviceCheckLatencyMs=15.71425 durationMs=16

2026-10-14T07:16:25.527Z
sa_server_request_failed
routePattern=/settings/user
errorCode=devicecheck_registration_http_failed
errorMessage="DeviceCheck registration failed (403)"
status=500

2026-10-14T07:16:25.534Z
sa_server_request_failed
routePattern=/accounts/check/{version}
errorCode=devicecheck_registration_http_failed
errorMessage="DeviceCheck registration failed (403)"
status=500

2026-10-14T07:17:28.060Z
[AppServerConnection] response_routed
method=configRequirements/read
errorCode=null durationMs=17
```

Other successful attestation generations were recorded at 07:16:20, 07:16:32, and 07:17:55 UTC. The settings and account-check failures recur at 07:18:27 UTC.

#### What was verified

- The local app-server connected over stdio at 07:15:35 UTC.
- `configRequirements/read` returned `errorCode=null` repeatedly, including at 07:15:46, 07:16:08, and 07:17:28 UTC.
- The separate durable app-server connection reached the connected state at 07:15:48 UTC.
- The local TOML configuration parses successfully.
- Read-only inspection of the installed application bundle shows a DeviceCheck registration POST to the configured `/devicecheck` endpoint. A non-success registration response produces `registration_http_failed`.
- The `status=500` entries above are from the desktop request layer propagating the registration failure. They do **not** by themselves establish that the upstream `/settings/user` and `/accounts/check` endpoints each returned HTTP 500.

#### Network/configuration context and limits

A local loopback HTTP/HTTPS/SOCKS proxy is configured on this Mac. No controlled alternate-proxy or alternate-network comparison has been completed, so the proxy is environment context, not an established cause.

The model provider uses Responses HTTP with `supports_websockets=false`. This setting does not control the desktop's separate durable app-server connection or DeviceCheck registration.

A provider display-name change intended to restore model-request compression was made at 04:28 UTC that day. The same `devicecheck_registration_http_failed` error was already present at 02:49:37 UTC, before that change. A separate model-endpoint diagnostic does not establish that desktop account/settings initialization is healthy.

Other requests in the same period returned `403 / cloudflare_challenge`. However, the DeviceCheck registration response body was not captured, so **I cannot establish that its 403 was itself a Cloudflare challenge**, or attribute it to an account restriction, proxy, OS defect, or application regression.

No cache/authentication-store deletion, device-verification bypass, application patch, or reinstall was performed as part of this investigation. Recovery of the affected new-chat window has not been verified.

#### Related reports and request

- #53333 — same application build and successful attestation followed by registration 403.
- #52746 — same registration error and blocked new chats.
- #51667 — similar workspace-settings UI, but its principal reports concern VM token-generation failures/timeouts. This machine's observed failure occurs **after successful token generation**.

Please investigate the registration-403 path and its effect on new-chat workspace initialization, and document supported recovery steps. This report provides additional versioned, timestamped evidence; please consolidate it with the existing registration-403 issue if appropriate.

Only selected, sanitized diagnostic metadata is included. No raw log files, credentials, account identifiers, private conversation content, project files, or original conversation IDs are attached.

items.title: macOS: hidden Page prewarm redirects the active chat to New chat (captured cross-window navigation)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: session
labels.description: Issues involving session (thread) management, resuming, forking, naming, archiving

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.1007.71326 (build 20398, production). Runtime call chain captured on 26.1007.30912 (build 20156).

### What subscription do you have?

Not specified.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS 15.6.1; uname -mprs: Darwin 24.6.0 arm64 arm

### What issue are you seeing?

The desktop app unexpectedly leaves the selected conversation and navigates the main window to the New chat/home route (`/`). Selecting the existing conversation again can be followed by another unsolicited jump. This interrupts normal use of existing chats.

On 2026-10-14, two separate transitions occurred 11.436 seconds apart (all timestamps below are UTC):

| Time | Main-window route |
| --- | --- |
| 06:24:05.617 | `/` — first unexpected jump |
| 06:24:10.344 | `/local/<thread-id>` — returned to the existing chat |
| 06:24:17.053 | `/` — second unexpected jump |
| 06:24:20.246 | `/local/<thread-id>` — returned again |

Adjacent duplicate owner-sync log entries were deduplicated; these are two transitions, not four. This recurrence was on build 20398 with an ordinary app launch, no debugging arguments, and the temporary diagnostic collector already stopped.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Open an existing conversation in the Codex desktop app and continue normal use. This installation uses both local and SSH-hosted conversations.
2. Intermittently, the main window switches to New chat without requesting a new chat.
3. Select the previous conversation again. In the observed October 14 occurrence, it was redirected again several seconds later.

A deterministic minimal trigger and a clean-profile reproduction are not established. The strongest diagnostic evidence is the captured hidden-Page navigation path below, rather than a reliably repeatable button sequence.

### What is the expected behavior?

The main window should remain on the selected conversation unless the user explicitly navigates. A hidden, unclaimed Page prewarm window should not forward its initialization redirects to the visible owner window or steal focus. Normal navigation from an intentionally opened Page should continue working.

### Additional information

### Captured mechanism on October 13

A 58.983-second local performance trace captured the occurrence ending at 07:40:18.972 UTC. The originating renderer's trace URL identified it as `/space/local-page-<redacted>?window=page&prewarm=1`; its window was hidden. CPU samples, correlated with the installed production bundles and main-window logs, showed:

```text
Hidden Page prewarm renderer:
React Router <Navigate> effect -> useNavigate -> router.replace
-> Mlc navigation interceptor -> SHa -> THa

Main process, 2.813 ms after the sampled renderer handoff:
navigateInOwnerWindow -> showWindow -> focus

Main-window log: ownerRoutePath=/
```

The installed main-process implementation forwards `navigate-to-route` to the owner and invokes `showWindow` with `stealFocus: true`. The 150 main-process samples belong to one short navigation operation, not 150 jumps.

Read-only inspection of build 20398 still finds the same relevant behavior: Page availability becoming disabled can render a replacement navigation to `/`, and non-Page/non-auth navigation from a Page window is handed to the owning main window. The October 14 first jump coincided with hidden-window initialization; a later Page-prewarm timeout reported `claimed=false editorReady=false`. That recurrence has log correlation, not a second captured call stack.

The exact runtime capability/availability/feature-gate branch selecting the original redirect was not captured. A Statsig bootstrap timeout preceded the October 13 occurrence, but no such timeout was logged in the current app process through the October 14 capture. A Statsig timeout is therefore not established as the root cause.

### Regression timing: verified update, uncertain first onset

The user recalls first noticing this after updating on October 8. Retained local logs confirm the version transition:

- October 8, 02:33:29 UTC: first retained launch of 26.1002.52244 (build 13536), following a process reporting 26.930.31730 (build 12947).
- October 9, 02:02:32 UTC: hidden-window initialization and a main-window home transition occur close together on 26.1007.21159 (build 20052); a Page-prewarm timeout follows at 02:04:27. This is an early related log pattern, not a captured stack.
- October 13: the cross-window navigation mechanism above was captured on build 20156.
- October 14: the two user-observed jumps above persisted on build 20398.

The old process also has home-route entries shortly before the October 8 update. Those logs cannot distinguish manual navigation from an unsolicited jump, and lack the later captured stack. Consequently, the update date is confirmed, but the first affected release and a causal regression in the October 8 update are not proven.

### Related reports

- #14411 and #17494 describe similar unexpected New chat navigation. This report adds macOS evidence and a captured hidden-Page-to-owner navigation path; please consolidate if maintainers confirm the same cause.
- #52093 concerns hidden Page prewarm conversation-resume/CPU looping, a different observed failure mode. A shared component alone does not establish the same bug.

Please investigate preventing an unclaimed hidden prewarm renderer's initialization redirect from navigating/focusing the owner window.

This report contains a sanitized diagnostic summary only. Conversation/page/account identifiers, SSH addresses, private paths, conversation content, raw logs and raw traces are omitted. The original evidence remains local.

### What issue are you seeing?

The MCP OAuth file store can load a stale duplicate record even after Codex successfully persisted the rotated successor under the current store key.

For an ordinary local MCP name, the file loader returns the first entry whose `server_name` and `server_url` match. It does not prefer the entry under `compute_store_key(server_name, url)`. The saver inserts the new credential under that computed key without removing another eligible record.

If an alternate matching key sorts first in the file's `BTreeMap`, this sequence results:

1. Both entries initially contain the same valid access/refresh pair.
2. Codex refreshes successfully and saves the successor under the current key.
3. The alternate entry retains the consumed predecessor.
4. A fresh process reads the alternate entry instead of the durable successor.
5. The provider rejects late predecessor reuse and invalidates the token family.
6. A subsequent process still reads the stale entry and receives `invalid_grant: session not found`.

This does **not** require concurrent app-server processes, missing refresh persistence, or an authenticated background SSE refresh. Sequential processes reproduce it.

The fixture uses the actual HQBase 1.4.0 auth/MCP modules with `@better-auth/oauth-provider` 1.7.0-rc.6 and a test-owned Miniflare D1 database. Only access-token TTL is shortened to 45 seconds. The 30-second refresh reuse interval and 30-day refresh lifetime remain unchanged. The MCP transport retains its JSON-response/stateless behavior.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Use only disposable homes, synthetic fixture credentials and an owned local OAuth/MCP server. Do not manipulate a real credential store or production grant.

1. Configure file-backed MCP OAuth storage and an ordinary server name, such as `example-mail`.
2. Complete a real authorization-code/PKCE flow against the owned fixture, then confirm a thread-scoped tool call succeeds.
3. In the test-owned `.credentials.json`, represent that same valid credential pair under two keys: the current computed key and an alternate key that sorts first. Both records have identical `server_name`, `server_url`, `issuer`, `client_id` and scopes.
4. For the observed key forms, the suffix comes from the SHA-256 prefix of the key payload serialized with sorted object keys versus insertion order (`type`, `url`, `headers`). These forms can differ with `serde_json` ordering features. For this test the duplicate initial state is constructed explicitly; no invalid token is injected.
5. Let the 45-second access token expire. Make a real thread-scoped MCP tool call through the app-server.
6. Observe a successful refresh and tool call. Verify privately that the current-key record now holds the persisted successor, while the alternate record still holds the consumed predecessor.
7. Stop that owned app-server. Wait beyond the provider's 30-second predecessor replay window and the saved access-token expiry. In our test, the post-rotation wait is 55 seconds.
8. Start a fresh app-server with the same owned home/config/store, without another login, and make the same MCP operation.
9. Observe `invalid_grant: invalid refresh token`, authorization-required failure, and provider-side family removal.
10. Start another fresh process against the same store. Observe the exact missing-record error: `invalid_grant: session not found`.

No provider rows are manually deleted, no token is manually revoked, and no rejection response is injected. Family removal follows the provider's actual late-reuse defense.

### Latest official 0.162.1 runtime validation

One bounded Mac dual-key trial failed and one single-key control passed:

| Case | Official Mac 0.162.1 result |
| --- | --- |
| Dual eligible keys; 60-second initial wait, successful real rotation, then 55-second post-rotation wait and fresh process | **RED 1/1**: successor persisted, stale alternate retained; `invalid_grant: invalid refresh token`; provider family becomes 0 access / 0 refresh rows while client and consent remain 1 each |
| Follow-up fresh process in that same dual trial | Exact `invalid_grant: session not found`, JSON-RPC `-32603`, authorization required |
| Single eligible key; same expiry/wait/restart chain | **GREEN, 0 failures / 1 trial**: later refresh and tool call succeed, saved successor remains active |

This latest run used the installed official binary and the real HQBase 1.4.0/provider 1.7.0-rc.6 fixture, without injected errors, pre-deletion or manual revocation. Setup failures and key-order discovery are not counted as trials. These small counts are observed trials, not statistical rate estimates.

**Build-dependent key ordering:** the Mac binary's own authorization write uses insertion order; the sorted form is its alternate. The earlier Linux binary used sorted order. The portable harness detects the current form from the actual write, then chooses a loopback port where the other verified form sorts first. It does not assume sorted order is current on every build. This reproduction constructs the duplicate state; it does not establish which historical process originally created a live alternate key.

### Observed controls — earlier Linux 0.159.1 runtime

| Initial store / timing | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Two eligible keys, 55-second post-rotation wait | Failure in 2/2 fresh-grant trials; token family becomes empty, while client and consent remain |
| Follow-up process after that natural family loss | Exact `invalid_grant: session not found` in 2/2 trials |
| Remove only the alternate key at fresh-grant setup; same expiry, waits and restart chain | Green, 0 failures / 1 trial; successor refreshes and tool calls succeed |
| Keep both keys, change only post-rotation wait from 55 seconds to 5 seconds | Green, 0 failures / 1 trial; actual second refresh was 7.641 seconds after the first, inside the 30-second replay window; family remains |

Earlier single-entry idle trials also passed twice, and a same-store sequential restart passed. Those controls confirm that ordinary refresh persistence works; the duplicate eligible entry is load-bearing in this reproduction.

### What is the expected behavior?

Reading and saving should agree on credential identity. A stale duplicate eligible record must not mask a successfully persisted successor under the current key.

In particular, an ordinary local MCP credential should not be chosen solely because its key sorts first. Handling legacy/alternate entries should resolve them consistently, so a later process cannot resurrect the consumed predecessor after a successful save.

"""Portable entry point. Run from an installed HQBase checkout containing v1.4.0.

No SSH, real profile, model turn or production endpoint. Mac child network is
restricted to loopback by sandbox-exec; all credentials/state are disposable.
"""
import hashlib
import json
import os
import pathlib
import select
import socket
import subprocess
import sys

HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
OUTPUT = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 'mcp-oauth-evidence').resolve()
OUTPUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)


def fixture(port):
    p = subprocess.Popen(['node', str(HERE / 'fixture.mjs'), str(port)],
                         stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, text=True)
    if not select.select([p.stdout], [], [], 40)[0]:
        p.terminate()
        raise RuntimeError('fixture startup timed out')
    state = json.loads(p.stdout.readline())
    if not state.get('fixtureReady'):
        p.terminate()
        raise RuntimeError('fixture unavailable')
    return p, state


def stop(p):
    p.terminate()
    try:
        p.wait(timeout=5)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        p.kill()
        p.wait()


def trial(port, mode):
    p = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, '-u', str(HERE / 'repro.py'), str(port), mode, str(OUTPUT)],
                         stdout=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
    rows = []
    with (OUTPUT / (mode + '.jsonl')).open('w') as log:
        for line in p.stdout:
            value = json.loads(line)
            rows.append(value)
            log.write(json.dumps(value) + '\n')
            log.flush()
            print(json.dumps(value), flush=True)
    p.wait()
    return rows


server = None
try:
    server, initial = fixture(0)
    discovery = trial(initial['port'], 'discover')
    order = next(row['observed_current_order'] for row in discovery if 'observed_current_order' in row)
    stop(server)
    server = None
    # Use the other observed serialization form; never forge an invalid credential.
    for port in range(53000, 53100):
        payload = {'type': 'http', 'url': f'http://127.0.0.1:{port}/mcp/full', 'headers': {}}
        keys = {name: hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=sort, separators=(',', ':')).encode()).hexdigest()[:16]
                for name, sort in [('sorted', True), ('insertion', False)]}
        alternate = 'sorted' if order == 'insertion' else 'insertion'
        if keys[alternate] >= keys[order]:
            continue
        with socket.socket() as s:
            try:

    (OUTPUT / 'summary.json').write_text(json.dumps({'current_order': order, 'results': results}, indent=2) + '\n')
finally:
    if server is not None:
        stop(server)

**Summary**

A command in an assistant-managed cloud environment fails before the requested program starts. The failure occurs when using the reviewed execution flow with sandbox_permissions="require_escalated".

**Error**
bwrap: Can't create file /home/agent/.codex/sessions: Read-only file system

**Observed behavior**
- The command returns exit code 1 immediately.
- No application output or HTTP response is produced.
- A subsequent retry produces the same error.
- Ordinary local commands worked during the investigation.
- No actionable approval-request ID was returned with the failed launch.

**Triggering operation**
The requested operation was a download of a public image asset. The error occurs before the download program starts, so no evidence currently links the failure to the destination website.

**Reproduction context**
1. Use the affected assistant-managed cloud environment.
2. Request an otherwise permitted command through exec_command with sandbox_permissions="require_escalated" and a task-specific justification.
3. Observe the bwrap initialization error before the requested program starts.
This describes the observed failure path, not a proven minimal reproduction. It has not been established that all escalated commands or other environments are affected.

**Expected behavior**
The command should either start through the supported approval flow or return a meaningful policy denial. Sandbox initialization should not fail while preparing a path unrelated to the requested operation.
Possible areas to investigate
- The generated bwrap arguments and filesystem mount layout.
- Whether the session directory or its parent is unexpectedly mounted read-only or missing during initialization.
- Differences between ordinary and escalated command-launch setup.
- Whether environment provisioning or restoration leaves an inconsistent mount configuration.
These are diagnostic leads, not confirmed root causes. Please preserve the intended isolation and access restrictions when fixing the issue.

**Impact**

A workflow requiring public-file downloads cannot continue through the affected execution path.

**Acceptance criteria**
- The affected environment can launch permitted commands through the supported review flow.
- Ordinary command execution continues to work.
- A permitted public-file download succeeds and produces a valid file.
- Protected session data remains inaccessible to task commands.
- Disallowed operations return an actionable denial rather than a sandbox initialization crash.

items.title: Isolate daemon package tests to reduce disk contention
items.body:
Isolate daemon package tests to reduce disk contention

## Why

Daemon package tests copy full debug CLI packages. Running these I/O-heavy cases alongside other tests can increase shared-disk writeback pressure.

## What changed

- Move package installation and replacement coverage into the `app_server_daemon_package` test binary, sharing daemon fixtures with the lifecycle tests.
- Reserve all nextest test threads for each package test and add an exclusive Bazel target that runs the cases serially on Linux and macOS.
- Hard-link the prepared fixture executable during package setup, while retaining real independent package copies in the installer.

items.body:
### Summary
The installed Codex desktop bundle appears to drop the realtime session recording eligibility flag before it reaches the existing recorder-enable setter.

### Environment and scope
macOS; installed bundle identity previously measured as com.openai.codex, app version 26.1007.41230 (build 20324). This report is based on read-only inspection of the installed app.asar on October 14, 2026. Minified symbol names below are specific to that inspected build.
This is a source-wiring report, not a claim that a live voice session was replayed or that current account eligibility was measured.

### Observed source path
1. Renderer function w_c dispatches electron-desktop-features-changed with realtimeSessionRecording: je.
2. The caller of main-process handler QXe supplies setRealtimeSessionRecordingEnabled: Be.setRealtimeSessionRecordingEnabled.
3. QXe's options destructuring does not consume setRealtimeSessionRecordingEnabled.
4. The electron-desktop-features-changed branch constructs the forwarded feature object without realtimeSessionRecording and invokes S(e, i.bundledPluginEligibilityReasons).
5. The supplied recorder-enable setter is not invoked in that handler.
6. The recorder gate (lue) initializes enabled to false. RealtimeSessionRecorder.record and readMostRecentSessionLog return early when recording is disabled.
7. readMostRecentSessionLog is used by feedback's desktop-log export for realtime-sessions/latest.jsonl.

### Expected
When the app's existing eligibility control permits recording, its existing main-process handler should forward that eligibility to the existing recorder-enable setter, including transitions back to disabled. Existing consent, privacy and eligibility constraints must be preserved.

### Actual / practical consequence
The inspected handler does not connect the already-sent flag to that setter. No realtime-sessions directory was present in the inspected local account, but directory absence alone does not prove this defect caused a particular missing transcript or that no voice call occurred.

### Minimal repair and verification request
Please confirm the maintainable source equivalent of this path, connect the existing eligibility flag to the existing setter if the omission is confirmed, and test:
- eligible/enabled session records the expected native session/thread/transcript events;
- disabled/ineligible session produces no recording;
- toggling eligibility invalidates stale recording generations as intended;
- feedback export includes the latest permitted diagnostic log while retaining existing audio/SDP redaction.

Separately, please clarify whether a supported native completed-turn/transcript reader is available to an installed local integration. Diagnostic export is not assumed to be such an interface. A downstream local integration crossing remains unproven.

No installed bundle was modified; no hidden IPC, recording toggle, microphone capture, service restart, or synthetic voice turn was used. No private conversation content, credentials, local user paths, or private evidence-ledger links are included in this report.

items.title: Reviewed Continue rejects equivalent backend findings after the UI entity key changes

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: safety-check
labels.description: Issues related to safety and abuse checks

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using?

| Inspected component | Version |
|---|---|
| macOS Desktop bundle | 26.1007.30912, build 20156 |
| Bundled Codex CLI | 0.162.0-alpha.17.2 |
| Remote Codex CLI inspected for the affected chats | 0.162.1 |

### What subscription do you have?

Subscription tier was not captured in the diagnostic evidence.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS on Apple Silicon, using Desktop Remote SSH conversations:

```text
Darwin 25.6.0 arm64 arm
```

The inspected environment includes managed account profiles and plugins. A clean stock-profile reproduction has not been performed.

### What issue are you seeing?

The Continue freshness guard can reject equivalent reviewed backend findings when a refreshed conversation snapshot replaces the failed turn's manager-local UI entity key. The backend turn and reviewed fields can remain equivalent while the dialog reports:

```text
Couldn't continue this chat. Close the dialog and review its latest status before trying again.
```

The history builder `X4t` assigns a local placeholder key using `createSearchIslandId`. Binding the backend turn through `Z4t` preserves that key. Different manager snapshots can therefore represent an equivalent backend failed turn with different local keys. The safety-review callback in `uXe` compares the captured UI entity key with the current entity key and rejects before continuation dispatch.

```text
review backend failed turn T and findings F under local key A
  -> equivalent snapshot represents T and F under local key B
  -> Continue freshness guard compares A with B
  -> rejection before dispatch
```

This is a review-validity identity defect, separated from the owner-selection and submission findings in [the existing remote-session issue](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/49892) and [its RCA response](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/49892#issuecomment-6159682917). The controlled rejection does not establish that new backend findings or a later backend status existed.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Affected-session UI sequence:

1. In a paused Remote SSH chat, open Review findings and read the findings.
2. Check the acknowledgement and click Continue chat.
3. The affected chat shows the error above and offers no identifiable later status to review.

The exact historical Continue exception was swallowed, so that click's failure path is not reconstructed. The constructible identity failure is isolated with the extracted installed guard and synthetic snapshots:

```sh
node review-identity-repro.mjs ./app-primary-6f60e9ac4103.js
```

Use the [sanitized review-identity reproduction](https://github.com/joshmouch/fork-openai-codex/blob/ad1b386e6e66bfea2ed4edb6da0430e1dee06fbe/diagnostics/remote-coordination-rca/review-identity-repro.mjs). Continuation dispatch is stubbed:

| Current state relative to reviewed state | Dispatch count | Result |
|---|---:|---|
| Captured UI key and reviewed fields retained | 1 | Passes the guard; dispatch stubbed |
| Replacement UI key; equivalent backend turn and reviewed fields | 0 | Rejects as no longer current |
| Reviewed findings changed | 0 | Rejects, as required |

The guard control proves rejection before dispatch. It does not claim live continuation acceptance or prove the original dialog failed through this comparison.

### What is the expected behavior?

Review validity should follow the stable backend review target or failed turn and the reviewed findings version/content. Equivalent snapshots should preserve that validity even when a renderer uses a different local presentation key.

Changed findings or a different backend review target must still invalidate the acknowledgement and require review. The repair direction is to separate stable review identity from manager-local view identity while preserving those safety checks; removing freshness validation would discard the required protection.

### Additional information

The demonstrated owner is the shipped Desktop history construction and review dialog. This investigation does not establish a public CLI/app-server defect or include a tested product patch.

| Installed asset | Relevant consumer |
|---|---|
| `webview/assets/app-shared-8bd9d0399038.js` | `X4t`, `Z4t`, manager-local history entry identity |
| `webview/assets/app-primary-6f60e9ac4103.js` | `uXe` review callback and Continue freshness guard |

| Extracted asset | SHA-256 |
|---|---|
| `app-primary-6f60e9ac4103.js` | 7fe9c00b03cb1de3ebc3a4bf298fc44b13a7fe67ca9cc335a9e2ecda969a1321 |
| `app-shared-8bd9d0399038.js` | 607ad0866dd25ed3764711b4467a9b60708353a599485b5249ff4cbe0e870245 |

[Sanitized handler controls](https://github.com/joshmouch/fork-openai-codex/blob/ad1b386e6e66bfea2ed4edb6da0430e1dee06fbe/diagnostics/remote-coordination-rca/sanitized-handler-controls.json) retain the controlled findings. The related [precautionary continuation report](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/43379) describes recurring safety pauses after Continue, without establishing this UI-key freshness condition.

items.title: Goal objective edits reject a healthy Remote SSH follower before thread/goal/set

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: app-server
labels.description: Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using?

| Inspected component | Version |
|---|---|
| macOS Desktop bundle | 26.1007.30912, build 20156 |
| Bundled Codex CLI | 0.162.0-alpha.17.2 |
| Remote Codex CLI inspected for the affected chats | 0.162.1 |

### What subscription do you have?

Subscription tier was not captured in the diagnostic evidence.

### What platform is your computer?

macOS on Apple Silicon, using Desktop Remote SSH conversations:

```text
Darwin 25.6.0 arm64 arm
```

The inspected environment includes managed account profiles and plugins. A clean stock-profile reproduction has not been performed.

### What issue are you seeing?

Editing a goal objective can fail while the viewing Desktop manager is a healthy follower of another conversation owner. The installed goal setter resumes the conversation for viewing, accepts a ready result, then requires the viewing manager to be the local owner before sending `thread/goal/set`.

The editor permits Save for a changed, nonempty objective when no save is pending. Its callback reaches `setThreadGoal` / `Q6t`; `Q6t` invokes `assertThreadFollowerOwner` after view resume. Despite its name, that assertion requires `getStreamRole(id).role === "owner"`. A ready follower therefore rejects before a goal-set RPC is sent.

```text
ready follower of a serviceable conversation owner
  -> change goal objective -> Save
  -> view resume reports ready
  -> local-owner assertion rejects
  -> no thread/goal/set request
```

This is a goal-objective mutation defect that does not require an unavailable client or failed recovery. It is separated from the owner-selection and submission findings in [the existing remote-session issue](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/49892) and [its RCA response](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/49892#issuecomment-6159682917).

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Affected-session UI sequence:

1. Open a Remote SSH chat with an editable goal while the viewing manager follows another conversation owner.
2. Open Edit, change the objective to nonempty text, and Save.
3. The affected chat reports a generic goal-save failure.

The UI sequence is reported behavior, not a deterministic clean-launch recipe. The exact historical goal exception was not captured. The failure condition is demonstrated separately by executing the extracted installed goal handler with synthetic state and stubbed collaborators:

```sh
node remote-coordination-repro.mjs ./app-shared-8bd9d0399038.js
```

Use the [sanitized reproduction script](https://github.com/joshmouch/fork-openai-codex/blob/ad1b386e6e66bfea2ed4edb6da0430e1dee06fbe/diagnostics/remote-coordination-rca/remote-coordination-repro.mjs). Its two `Q6t` controls isolate goal objective saving:

| Handler input | Goal-set RPC count | Result |
|---|---:|---|
| View resume returns ready; manager is owner | 1 | Stubbed request completes and goal state updates |
| View resume returns ready; manager is healthy follower | 0 | Local-owner assertion rejects before RPC |

These controls prove the Desktop consumer rejection. They do not claim a successful live server mutation or establish the exact historical UI exception. The `/goal` command mapping, goal status changes and goal clearing are outside this control's demonstrated scope.

### What is the expected behavior?

A goal objective edit from a readable follower chat should execute through the current serviceable conversation owner. View readiness should not be interpreted as local mutation authority.

The repair direction is to resolve the mutation's execution owner and forward the goal edit through that owner, retaining the operation's delivery identity and outcome. The owner-side authority check should remain meaningful. Forcing the viewing window to seize ownership would conflate viewing with execution authority.

### Additional information

The demonstrated owner is the shipped Desktop goal editor and conversation manager. This investigation does not establish a defect in the public Rust CLI/app-server implementation or include a tested product patch.

| Installed asset | Relevant consumer |
|---|---|
| `webview/assets/app-primary-6f60e9ac4103.js` | Goal editor Save eligibility and callback |
| `webview/assets/app-shared-8bd9d0399038.js` | `Q6t` and local-owner assertion |

| Extracted shared asset | SHA-256 |
|---|---|
| `app-shared-8bd9d0399038.js` | 607ad0866dd25ed3764711b4467a9b60708353a599485b5249ff4cbe0e870245 |

[Sanitized handler controls](https://github.com/joshmouch/fork-openai-codex/blob/ad1b386e6e66bfea2ed4edb6da0430e1dee06fbe/diagnostics/remote-coordination-rca/sanitized-handler-controls.json) retain the consumer results. The related [SSH goal report](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/25455) concerns an attachments-related error; that report does not establish this ready-follower owner assertion failure.

The Windows ChatGPT desktop app with Codex repeatedly reloads to a white screen and interrupts dictation when opening and scrolling a large existing Codex chat. Agent execution is not required: this was reproduced while the agent was idle.

Environment:

- System-managed page file approximately 16 GB. Windows had available physical and paging-backed memory during investigation.
- Previous MSIX package OpenAI.Codex 26.1007.2314.0.
- Updated through Microsoft Store to OpenAI.Codex 26.1007.9446.0; confirmed the running executable belonged to the new package.
- Existing chat transcript approximately 4.38 GB. Private conversation content is not included.

Reproduction:
1. Launch the updated app.
2. Open the large existing Codex chat.
3. Scroll earlier messages and use dictation while the agent is idle.
4. Observe renderer private memory increasing and the interface reloading to a white screen, interrupting dictation.

Observed renderer private memory in the updated build:
1.15 GB shortly after opening; 2.44 GB after about one minute; then 3.45 GB; briefly dropped to 2.92 GB; later reached 4.51 GB within approximately three minutes.
Aggregate app private memory rose from about 2.56 GB to 6.45 GB.

Confirmed diagnostic on 14 October 2026:
Electron renderer process gone reason=oom exit_code=-536870904
After crash/recovery, the observed renderer PID disappeared and aggregate app private memory fell to approximately 2.43 GB.
Repeated ResizeObserver loop errors appeared beforehand; their causal role has not been established.

Previously attempted without resolving this reproduction:
- Restarting the application and removing saved browser restoration records.
- Launching the earlier version with --js-flags=--max-old-space-size=8192 (flag propagation verified; actual effective V8 ceiling not measured).
- Microsoft Store app update.

Expected: Existing history should be paged/rendered with bounded memory, and dictation should remain usable. The user needs to preserve this existing chat, notes and code rather than start over.

Requested investigation: determine which history/rendering allocations grow during opening and scrolling, and address the renderer OOM. This report establishes the failure and reproduction but does not identify the exact leaking or over-allocating code.

This report excludes usernames, local paths, chat IDs, repository names, credentials, conversation contents and raw logs. No attachments are required for the initial public issue.
